Museu de Arte Moderna de São Paulo.note: Sponsorship = Patroc. Incentivo Federal 12,721,759 + Estadual 958,700 + Municipal 1,839,659 (tax-incentive sponsorship by companies). Private = that plus donations 3,734,977. Earned = activity income 3,520,021 before returns of 2,089 and taxes of 375,464. 'Other revenues' of 11,408,067 are almost all gratuities and volunteer work 11,345,338, booked as both revenue and expense, so cash income is about 24.2 million. Financial income 1,728,047 also in income. The statements carry no government grant line, so public is null. Surplus 3,775,286.

Glenbow.basis: Glenbow-Alberta Institute audited financial statements, year ended 31 March 2026 (Grant Thornton): statement of operations, Operating Fund, p. 4 (PDF p. 6); note 12 grants and subsidies; statement of financial position p. 3; restricted and revitalization fund statements p. 5
Glenbow.line: FY2025-26 operating revenue CAD 5.1M: about 58 percent Alberta government and public grants, 39 percent donations, sponsorships and memberships; operating deficit 1.7M (audited statements, p. 4).
Glenbow.note: Operating Fund only. Public = Government of Alberta 2,288,000 + grants and subsidies 672,103 (Calgary Arts Development 465,575, provincial Other Initiatives 206,528). Private is donations, sponsorships and memberships together; sponsorship is not stated separately. Earned is retail sales and rentals 23,000; other income 140,007 and amortization of deferred contributions 10,936 not classified. Capital-campaign money sits outside this figure: Restricted Funds revenue 20,081,850 (donations 14,750,000, investment income 5,331,850) and Revitalization Fund revenue 10,272,048 (government capital grants 6,332,887, campaign contributions 3,705,820). Net assets are total fund balances 218,956,659, mostly the revitalized building.

The Rooms.basis: The Rooms Corporation Annual Report 2025-26, Appendix A audited statements, Statement of Operations (PDF p. 88: province operating grants 6,883,495, employee-benefit contributions 823,485, capital grant 217,582, commercial operations 2,332,378, Government of Canada 759,925, corporate sponsorship 102,263, external funding 38,144); statement of financial position (PDF p. 87)
The Rooms.line: FY2025-26 revenue CAD 11.2M: about 78 percent provincial and federal government, 21 percent commercial operations, 1 percent corporate sponsorship; deficit 486,495 (audited statements, PDF p. 88).
The Rooms.note: Provincial Crown corporation. Public = province 7,924,562 (operating grants, employee-benefit contribution, capital grant) + Government of Canada 759,925. Private shows only corporate sponsorship; external funding 38,144 is not classified and donations are not on the face statement. Corporate sponsorship fell from 347,367 in 2024-25. The statements are scanned images, read from the page images.

Kunsten Museum of Modern Art Aalborg.n: Kunsten Museum of Modern Art Aalborg
Kunsten Museum of Modern Art Aalborg.basis: Kunsten Årsberetning 2023 (web report), Årsregnskab 31 Dec 2023 shown as images: Driftsindtægter notes 1 to 10 (Aalborg Kommune 17,184,020; Statstilskud 2,700,190; Puljetilskud 170,000; Regionale tilskud 225,450; Ikke offentlige tilskud 9,934,432; Entré og publikumsklub 6,480,416; Erhvervsklubmedlemsskaber 1,995,634; Butik 4,203,370; Café 7,142,289), balance note 25 egenkapital
Kunsten Museum of Modern Art Aalborg.line: FY2023 income DKK 51.8M: about 39 percent public grants, 23 percent foundation grants and business-club memberships, 36 percent entry, shop, cafe and rentals (annual report 2023, accounts images).
Kunsten Museum of Modern Art Aalborg.note: Latest accounts it publishes: the 2024 and 2025 reports on its site carry no accounts. Read from images on the page. The accounts run the museum's own operations; the Aalborg municipal grant includes 3,999,996 passed on to Utzon Center. Public = municipality + state + state pool 170,000 + regional EU-project grant 225,450. Private = non-public grants 9,934,432 (foundations such as Augustinus Fonden, Det Obelske Familiefond, Ny Carlsbergfondet named per exhibition, no amounts) + business-club memberships 1,995,634. Earned = entry and public club 6,480,416 (not split) + shop + cafe + room rental 405,650 + tours 186,016. Diverse income 1,219,982 not classified. Result 112,659.

Ordrupgaard.basis: Årsrapport 2025, Tabel 5 Resultatopgørelse (PDF p. 18: Bevilling 19,200.0; Salg af varer og tjenesteydelser 13,236.7; Tilskud til egen drift 8,187.4 thousand DKK); Tabel 19 (PDF p. 30: private fonde 7,857.8; statslige fonds- og programmidler 329.6); Tabel 8 egenkapital
Ordrupgaard.line: FY2025 income DKK 40.6M: about 48 percent state appropriation and public programme funds, 19 percent private foundation grants, 33 percent sales (annual report 2025, PDF pp. 18 and 30).
Ordrupgaard.note: State museum under the Ministry of Culture; statements follow the state accounting format. Public is the state appropriation 19,200,000 plus state fund and programme money 329,600. Expenditure is ordinary operating costs; interest on state loan 1,838,900 comes on top, and other operating income 24,000 is outside income_total. Surplus 1,277,200. Private foundations are not named in the table, so Augustinus Fonden's share cannot be isolated. Prior year (2024) income was 68,570,400 because foundations funded major art acquisitions.

HEART Herning.basis: Årsrapport 2023 (BDO audited), Resultatopgørelse p. 10 (PDF p. 11: Entré 559,284; Forretningsenheder, bidrag 114,156; Tilskud mv. 16,233,803; Indtægter i alt 16,907,243); Balance p. 11 (Egenkapital 2,099,379)
HEART Herning.line: FY2023 income DKK 16.9M: about 96 percent grants and support (state, Herning Municipality, foundations, sponsors), about 4 percent admissions and shop contribution (audited statements 2023, p. 10).
HEART Herning.note: The PDF is image-only, read from page images. The single line Tilskud mv. 16,233,803 does not split public from private; management review lists the state Slots- og Kulturstyrelsen and Herning Kommune (multi-year operating grants), more than a dozen foundations and state funds (A.P. Moller, Augustinus, Ny Carlsberg, Obel, Ole Kirk's, Statens Kunstfond and others) and business sponsors, with no amounts. Earned is Entré plus Forretningsenheder bidrag. Result 75,465. 2024 report not published on its page.

Trapholt.note: trapholt.dk returned a browser check page (HTTP 454, Checking your browser) for both the annual report list and the 2025 annual report PDF, so nothing was read. The Danish company register search (distribution.virk.dk) returned no filings for CVR 11527132. The only other accounts found are a 2005 ministry review with 2004 figures, too old to use.

Kiran Nadar Museum of Art.basis: KNMA FCRA financial statements for the year ended 31 March 2025 (V. Nagarajan & Co.): Income and Expenditure Account (PDF p. 4: donation 4,93,34,33,099; other income 37,78,326), Receipt and Payment Account (p. 5), Balance Sheet (p. 3)
Kiran Nadar Museum of Art.line: FY2024-25 foreign-contribution account only: INR 4.93 billion in donations received, INR 4.20 billion spent buying artwork; no full museum accounts are published (FCRA statement, year to 31 March 2025).
Kiran Nadar Museum of Art.note: Only the special-purpose FCRA statement is on its site; it covers the account that holds foreign contributions, not the whole museum, so income_total, expenditure, public and earned are left null. Donations (Indian digit grouping 4,93,34,33,099) are the foreign contributions received, INR 4,933,433,099 against 6,02,46,95,000 (INR 6.02 billion) in 2024. Spending in the account is almost all artwork purchases of 4,19,93,75,356 plus advances for artwork 75,56,08,206, booked as investments; operating spending was only 39,00,473. Net assets are the corpus fund 14,78,37,07,232 plus general fund 16,08,58,16,744, with artwork held at cost of 29,39,50,58,642. Other income 37,78,326 is interest. Free-entry museum; the non-FCRA accounts that would show public or earned income are not published.

IMMA.basis: IMMA Financial Statements 2025 (signed, with auditor's certificate): Statement of Income and Expenditure and Retained Revenue Reserves, p. 12 (PDF p. 12); notes 3 to 6; statement of financial position, total net assets
IMMA.line: FY2025 income EUR 12.4M: about 69 percent Oireachtas grant, 17 percent deferred pension funding, 10 percent commercial, 3 percent sponsorship; deficit 54,587 (audited statements, p. 12).
IMMA.note: State body funded by the Department of Culture, Communications and Sport. Public is the Oireachtas grant 8,511,054; the net deferred pension funding of 2,105,481 is a matching accounting entry for State-funded pensions (retirement costs 2,104,235 are in expenditure) and is not counted as public or in any category. Earned is commercial activities (hire of premises and meadows, bookshop, car park, franchise) 1,274,133; arts programme receipts 103,406 not classified. Donated artworks are booked through a capital account (645,909 in 2025), not income. Net assets include the building and the collection.

Beppu Contemporary Art Festival.basis: Beppu Art Month 2014 project report (executive committee of the Beppu Contemporary Art Festival Mixed Bathing World, 27 April 2015), chapter 4, 収支実績表 (PDF p. 30): Beppu City 1,000,000; Oita Prefectural Arts Festival grant 380,000; Fukutake Foundation 1,030,000; local firms 800,000; other income 761,786
Beppu Contemporary Art Festival.line: FY2014 income JPY 3.97M for the committee's Beppu Art Month: about 35 percent city and prefecture grants, 46 percent foundation and sponsors, 13 percent fees (project report).
Beppu Contemporary Art Festival.note: Oldest figures in this batch and not the festival edition itself: it is the Beppu Art Month 2014 programme run by the Mixed Bathing World executive committee; no later accounts were found on beppuproject.com or by search. Public = Beppu City 1,000,000 + Oita Prefectural Arts Festival grant 380,000. Private = Fukutake Foundation 1,030,000 + local-business sponsors 800,000. Earned = participant registration fees 275,000 + project fees 245,000. Rest is venue fees held for organisers 207,000, miscellaneous 3,500 and carry-over 31,286. Surplus 35,902.

Aichi Triennale.basis: Aichi Triennale 2025 report, VII Organising committee status, 1 Income and expenditure (report p. 135-137; PDF pp. 138-140): 2025 income by category, budget figures
Aichi Triennale.line: FY2025 budget JPY 1.29 billion: about 88 percent public contributions (Aichi Prefecture, Seto City), 10 percent tickets, 2 percent sponsorship and grants (2025 report, budget).
Aichi Triennale.note: These are the budgeted 2025 figures; the report says the 2025 settlement was not final as of March 2026. Actuals it does give: 2023 income 42,484 thousand and 2024 income 137,315 thousand, essentially all from Aichi Prefecture (137,262,440 yen in 2024). Public = Aichi Prefecture 1,130,866,000 + Seto City 5,000,000. The 26,799,000 line is corporate sponsorship donations plus national and foundation grants, not split, so private and sponsorship are null. Earned = ticket income 124,529,000 (contemporary art 113,398,000, performing arts 11,131,000) + miscellaneous 656,000. The report lists 124 supporters (48 donating companies and 48 ticket purchasers) without amounts.

Museum of Contemporary Art Tokyo.basis: MOT annual report FY2024 (令和6年度), Part III, 2 budget overview by project (PDF p. 114): public-interest projects 1,030,956 + 299,015 thousand yen and profit-making projects 12,604 thousand yen
Museum of Contemporary Art Tokyo.line: FY2024 budget for the museum JPY 1.34 billion across public-interest and shop and restaurant projects; no income split is published for the museum itself (annual report FY2024, p. 113).
Museum of Contemporary Art Tokyo.note: The museum is run by the Tokyo Metropolitan Foundation for History and Culture and has no separate accounts, so income is null; expenditure is the sum of the budget lines (not actual spending): commissioned-account projects 1,030,956 thousand, former general-account projects 299,015 thousand, profit-making projects 12,604 thousand. Visitors FY2024 758,066. For the whole foundation (all its museums and theatres) FY2025 statements show revenue 28,951,311,081: about 65 percent management commissions (18.81 billion) from Tokyo, 9 percent subsidies, 10 percent business income, donations only 10 million; this is not museum-specific (rekibun.or.jp R7 statements).

Cairns Art Gallery.basis: ACNC 2024 Annual Information Statement dataset (data.gov.au), Cairns Art Gallery Precinct Ltd, ABN 45062537259, year 1 July 2023 to 30 June 2024: revenue from government, donations and bequests, revenue from goods and services, total gross income, total expenses, net assets
Cairns Art Gallery.line: FY2023-24 income AUD 2.3M: about 59 percent government, 5 percent donations, 34 percent goods and services; surplus 316,530 (ACNC AIS 2024).
Cairns Art Gallery.note: Two ACNC charities carry the name: Cairns Art Gallery Precinct Ltd (the operating gallery, used here) and the separate Cairns Art Gallery Foundation Limited (art-purchase fundraising, income 32,744). The acnc.gov.au page in the input timed out, so the match is by name, not by the page's identifier. Revenue from goods and services 769,542 is not split by the AIS, so any sponsorship in it cannot be separated. Net assets are high because of the gallery building and revaluation (other comprehensive income 505,707).

National Gallery of Australia.note: nga.gov.au answered HTTP 403 and infrastructure.gov.au (where the gallery's Portfolio Budget Statements sit) timed out or dropped the connection, so no annual report or statements were read. A web search summary of the 2025-26 Portfolio Budget Statements quotes 69,917 thousand AUD of government appropriation as the 2024-25 estimated actual and 20,548 thousand AUD from other sources; I could not open the document to confirm, and these are budget estimates, not audited figures, so they are not entered.

National Art Gallery of The Bahamas.n: National Art Gallery of The Bahamas
National Art Gallery of The Bahamas.basis: NAGB audited financial statements, year ended 30 June 2024 (Baker Tilly): Statement of Comprehensive Income/(Loss), p. 4 (PDF p. 6); Statement of Financial Position, p. 3 (PDF p. 5); notes 6, 10, 11
National Art Gallery of The Bahamas.line: FY2023-24 income BSD 1.57M: about 83 percent government grant and paid utilities, 9 percent private grants and donations, 8 percent tickets, shop and rentals (audited statements).
National Art Gallery of The Bahamas.note: Income_total is revenue 1,504,509 plus other income 62,553 (facility rentals and special tours, interest). Public = government grant 1,240,000 + government subsidy 62,706 (costs the government paid directly, note 6(c)). Private = deferred private grants released 134,533 + funding and donations 2,789. Earned = ticket and gift shop sales 64,481 + other income 62,553. Net income 96,508. Statements are scanned images, read from page images. Latest year posted; the year to June 2025 is not on the site yet.

WIELS.note: The Belgian National Bank register lists WIELS Centre d'Arts Contemporains (enterprise 0478.422.608) with abridged-model accounts filed for 2025, 2024 and 2023, but the register's accounting-data and PDF endpoints returned 403, so no figure was read. wiels.org and its partners page publish no annual report or budget.

Museo Nacional de Arte de Bolivia.n: Museo Nacional de Arte de Bolivia
Museo Nacional de Arte de Bolivia.basis: Fundación Cultural del Banco Central de Bolivia, Estado de Recursos y Gastos Corriente Comparativo 31 Dec 2025 (SIGEP, PDF pp. 1-2: recursos corrientes 49,509,590.76; transferencias corrientes del sector público financiero 44,826,616.54; venta de bienes y servicios 4,468,995.77; gastos corrientes 55,293,516.03); Balance General (patrimonio 298,965,884.20)
Museo Nacional de Arte de Bolivia.line: FY2025 current income BOB 49.5M for the foundation that runs the museum: about 91 percent transfers from the public financial sector, 9 percent sales; expenses 55.3M (FCBCB statements 2025).
Museo Nacional de Arte de Bolivia.note: The museum has no separate accounts: these are the Fundación Cultural del Banco Central de Bolivia, which runs the Museo Nacional de Arte and other cultural sites, so the figures cover all of them. Public is the current transfer from the public financial sector (the Central Bank); donations were 0 in 2025 (12,193 in 2024). Other income 213,978 (fines and miscellaneous). Result for 2025 a loss of 5,783,925.27. Scanned statements read from page images. Capital spending is not in this statement.

Pinacoteca de São Paulo.basis: APAC Plano Orçamentário Consolidado CG 5/2023, 2025 (xlsx and pdf on apacsp.org.br), Demonstração de Resultado: rows 4 Total de Receitas 74,320,044.46; 4.1 Receita de Repasse Apropriada 39,774,125.13; 4.2 Receita de Captação Apropriada 33,675,464.09; 6 Total de Despesas
Pinacoteca de São Paulo.line: FY2025 income BRL 74.3M under state management contract: about 54 percent state transfer, 16 percent tickets, rentals and shop, 29 percent incentive-law and partner fundraising (APAC budget report 2025).
Pinacoteca de São Paulo.note: Associação Pinacoteca Arte e Cultura runs the Pinacoteca and the Memorial da Resistência together under state contract CG 005/2023; this is the consolidated management-contract result, not audited statements, and cannot be split between the two museums. Income equals expenditure because the contract balances. Public = repasse appropriated 39,774,125.13 (cash received 53,561,313 for the year). Captação incentivada 21,356,803.46 comes from incentive laws and calls for proposals (PROAC state, FINEP federal) not split between public and private, so private and sponsorship are null; partnerships 79,690; financial income 870,455.24. Earned = tickets, rentals and shop 12,238,970.63.

Art Gallery of Alberta.basis: 2025 Report to the Community, p. 55 (PDF p. 55), Revenues and Expenses: operating revenue 5,460,185; Grants - Operating 2,313,400; Fundraising 1,536,802; Memberships 86,478; Admissions 175,568; Fees and programming 288,455; Retail 330,070
Art Gallery of Alberta.line: FY2025 operating revenue CAD 5.5M: about 42 percent operating grants, 30 percent fundraising and memberships, 15 percent admissions, programmes and retail; expenses 5.7M (Report to the Community 2025, p. 55).
Art Gallery of Alberta.note: Summary in the annual report, not the audited statements (the report says audited statements exist; they were not on the page, and the CRA T3010 page could not be opened here). Public is operating grants only, from City of Edmonton, Edmonton Arts Council, Alberta Foundation for the Arts and Canada Council. TREX/Projects/Programs grants 306,723 are not split public or private and are left out. Private is Fundraising 1,536,802 plus Memberships 86,478; fundraising includes gala and auction money and sponsorship, not split. Earned is admissions + fees and programming + retail. Other revenue 422,689. Deficit 224,187.

Musée d'art de Joliette.basis: Rapport annuel 2024-2025, états financiers au 31 août 2025 (DCA, auditor's report 16 Dec 2025): Résultats (PDF p. 121, report p. 119); annexes A, B, D, E (PDF pp. 136-137); Évolution de l'actif net (PDF p. 122)
Musée d'art de Joliette.line: FY2024-25 (to 31 August 2025) revenue CAD 3.2M: about 43 percent government and city grants, 23 percent donations and sponsorship, 12 percent earned; deficit 38,447 (audited).
Musée d'art de Joliette.note: Public = government grants 1,237,406 (Quebec 898,766, Canada 338,640 including Canada Council 205,000) + City of Joliette 138,533. Other grants from unnamed organisations 289,548 are in neither category. Private: 652,520 of the 740,384 in donations and sponsorship came from the Fondation du Musée d'art de Joliette, a related foundation. Income includes 387,623 amortization of deferred capital contributions. Earned (Annexe A) includes small membership and fundraising items. Net assets are a deficit of 115,015.

Kunsthalle Praha.basis: Výroční zpráva 2025, účetní závěrka: výkaz zisku a ztráty (Provozní dotace 0, Přijaté příspěvky 74,608, Tržby za vlastní výkony a zboží 32,655, Ostatní výnosy 366, Výnosy celkem 107,629 thousand CZK), PDF p. 39; rozvaha, Vlastní zdroje celkem; notes p. 44
Kunsthalle Praha.line: FY2025 income CZK 107.6M: about 69 percent donations (nearly all from the Pudil Family Foundation), 30 percent earned, no operating subsidy (annual report 2025, PDF pp. 39 and 44).
Kunsthalle Praha.note: Foundation fund (nadační fond), unaudited small-entity statements. The note says the 74,608 thousand CZK main-activity loss is covered by a gift from the Pudil Family Foundation, its founder; REN Power CZ a.s. gave 2,500 thousand CZK. Other income 366 thousand CZK not in any category. Net assets are Vlastní zdroje at year end (17,060 thousand CZK). Result for 2025 was a loss of 2,493 thousand CZK.

ARoS.basis: Årsrapport 2025, PDF p. 25 (resultatopgørelse: Omsætning, Offentlige tilskud, Sponsorer og fonde, Indtægter) and p. 27 (notes 1 to 3); balance sheet note 8 egenkapital
ARoS.line: FY2025 income DKK 163.6M: about 51 percent earned, 31 percent public grants, 18 percent sponsors and foundations (annual report 2025, PDF pp. 25 and 27).
ARoS.note: Expenditure is the sum of the stated cost lines (exhibitions 73,801,216; other external 44,684,425; salaries 39,098,819; depreciation 4,412,712; interest 18,046); the report gives no single total. Sponsorship left null because the report merges sponsors and foundations (main sponsors and business clubs 10,643,140; project sponsors 14,793,518; art-purchase and research grants 3,620,706). Public includes municipal 17,890,100, state via Aarhus 31,375,025, direct state 1,000,000. Auditor statement covers the Ministry of Culture operating grant.

Copenhagen Contemporary.basis: Årsrapport 2024, resultatopgørelse (PDF p. 26: Nettoomsætning 41,056,544; Andre driftsindtægter 1,269,180), note 1 (PDF p. 30: public grants), ledelsesberetning (PDF p. 25: fondsstøtte 25,799 t.kr.), egenkapitalopgørelse (PDF p. 29)
Copenhagen Contemporary.line: FY2024 income DKK 42.3M: about 26 percent public grants, 61 percent foundation support, the rest sales, rentals and other income (annual report 2024, PDF pp. 25 to 30).
Copenhagen Contemporary.note: income_total is net turnover 41,056,544 plus other operating income 1,269,180 (VAT compensation 539,405, wage refunds 729,775). Expenditure is the sum of all stated cost lines including financial costs; result 1,024,915. Public = Statens Kunstfond 543,672 + Ministry of Culture 5,308,334 + City of Copenhagen 5,000,000. Private is the foundation support the management review states (25,799 thousand DKK); in-kind sponsorship is mentioned but not valued. Earned income is not given as a figure. Augustinus Fonden gave a donation for an exhibition.

Kunsthal Charlottenborg.basis: Kunstakademiets Billedkunstskoler Årsrapport 2024, Tabel 3 (PDF p. 13), row Kunsthal Charlottenborg: bevilling (FL+TB) 12,316.4, øvrige indtægter 8,553.4, omkostninger 20,203.5 thousand DKK
Kunsthal Charlottenborg.line: FY2024 Kunsthal Charlottenborg income DKK 20.9M: about 59 percent state appropriation, 41 percent other income, mostly grants to its own operations (Academy annual report 2024, PDF p. 13).
Kunsthal Charlottenborg.note: Kunsthal Charlottenborg has no accounts of its own; it is one task inside the state-funded Royal Danish Academy of Fine Arts schools (hovedkonto 21.41.09), so these are the Academy's allocation for the Kunsthal. The report says the Kunsthal drew a large share of the other income from grants to own operations (not split by funder or amount) and gives no sales figure. Result for the task was an underspend of 666,300. Private and earned left null because the report does not split them.

Ny Carlsberg Glyptotek.basis: Årsregnskab 2025 (signed Penneo copy), Resultatopgørelse for året 2025 (printed p. 12, PDF p. 14): Tilskud 69,085,275 plus Indtægter 67,903,634; Balance (pp. 13-14); notes 1 to 4 (pp. 15-16).
Ny Carlsberg Glyptotek.line: FY2025 income DKK 137.0M: about 23 percent state grants, 28 percent foundations and donations, 42 percent tickets, events and shop (årsregnskab 2025, p. 12).
Ny Carlsberg Glyptotek.note: Income is Tilskud plus Indtægter as the statement sets them out. Public is the Danish Agency for Culture and Palaces (SLKS) operating grant 31,063,206 plus project grants 245,998. Private is Ny Carlsbergfondet operating grant 14,660,000, donations 44,297 and project and exhibition support from foundations 23,071,774 (Ny Carlsbergfondet 14,868,384, Carlsbergfondet 1,014,543, Aage and Johanne Louis-Hansen 3,256,619, Det Obelske Fond 1,480,116 and others; Statens kunstfond gave 0). Earned is tickets 41,304,278, events 9,464,607 and shop and cafe 7,362,599. Not counted: other income 9,564,730 (including VAT refund and compensation 4,185,641) and interest 207,420. Equity 31,074,473.

Louisiana Museum of Modern Art.basis: Årsrapport 2025 (signed 12 May 2026), Resultatopgørelse (printed p. 37, PDF p. 38): Nettoomsætning 105,723, Andre driftsposter 1,579, Offentlige tilskud (Kulturstyrelsen) 36,529, Andre eksterne omkostninger, Personaleomkostninger, Afskrivninger; Balance (p. 39); notes 1, 6, 10.
Louisiana Museum of Modern Art.line: FY2025 income DKK 143.8M before art-purchase grants: about 25 percent Kulturstyrelsen grant; the other 75 percent, net revenue of 105.7M, is not split in the report (årsrapport 2025, p. 37).
Louisiana Museum of Modern Art.note: Figures are TDKK in the report, converted. Income is net revenue 105,723 plus other operating items 1,579 plus the Kulturstyrelsen grant 36,529. Expenditure is external costs 56,705, staff 75,085 and depreciation 1,234, and excludes art purchases of 88,336 (73,063 fully donor-funded, 9,300 partly, 5,973 unfunded) and finance costs 599. Grants and donations for art purchases of 82,363 sit below the result line and are not counted in income. The report does not split net revenue into tickets, sponsorship, donations or sales: the cafe, shop and web shop are run by Louisiana-Fonden (note 10). Private, sponsorship and earned are therefore null. Other income excluded: finance income 955, gain on sale 120. Equity (overført resultat) 22,779. The funding text cites a 2024 Kulturstyrelsen grant of 36.1M; 2025 is 36.5M.

Ludwig Museum Budapest.basis: Éves költségvetési beszámoló 2025 (PIR 329134, generated 16 March 2026): form 02 B1-B7 költségvetési bevételek (PDF p. 6), form 04 B8 finanszírozási bevételek (p. 7), form 01 K1-K8 költségvetési kiadások (p. 5), form 12/A Mérleg, G) Saját tőke (pp. 15-16).
Ludwig Museum Budapest.line: FY2025 income HUF 743.8M: about 66 percent state funding, 13 percent company and foreign donors, 21 percent own revenue (éves költségvetési beszámoló 2025, forms 01, 02, 04).
Ludwig Museum Budapest.note: The museum is a state budgetary institution. Income is B1-B7 revenue 323,197,037 plus central, supervisory-body support (B816) 420,554,227; the 29,457,139 of prior-year surplus drawn on is not counted, so total financing is 773,208,403. Public is the central support plus 70,400,000 of operating grants from separated state funds (B16). Private is other operating transfers received (B65) 97,070,777: financial companies 31,000,000, other enterprises 31,350,000, other foreign sources 32,689,467, church bodies 2,000,000, households 31,310; sponsorship is not split out. MAC Montréal.line: FY2024-25 income CAD 16.9M: about 79 percent Quebec and federal grants, 9 percent donations and sponsorship, 2 percent donated art, 2 percent earned (audited statements, p. 200).
MAC Montréal.note: Audited by the Auditor General of Quebec. Public is Quebec grants 13,015,643 (operating 12,535,454 plus capital 480,189) plus Canada grants 346,027. Private is Commandites et autres dons 1,522,705: cash gifts 1,400,471 (1,398,872 of it from the museum's own Foundation), cash sponsorship 21,311, gifts in kind of advertising 100,923. Donated artworks 403,690 are booked as income and expense and are in none of the three. Earned is catalogue sales 6,421, space rental 35,824, ticketing and memberships 323,048, education and culture 14,903; memberships cannot be separated from tickets. Project cost recoveries 665,724, investment income 467,588 and other 101,950 are in none. Expenses 16,114,416 gave an excess of 789,107. Net assets 2,520,157 include endowment 1,662,846.

The Polygon Gallery.basis: Annual report 2024, audited financial statements of The British Columbia Photography and Media Arts Society (Tompkins Wozny), printed as page images: Statement of Operations (printed p. 49), Statement of Financial Position (p. 47), note 12 government grant revenues (PDF p. 59), Treasurer's report p. 43.
The Polygon Gallery.line: FY2024 income CAD 5.4M: about 14 percent government grants, 30 percent donations, sponsorship and events, 41 percent earned (audited statements, annual report p. 49).
The Polygon Gallery.note: Calendar year 2024. Public is government grants 934,204 less 170,613 of in-kind permissive tax exemption from the City of North Vancouver, which is tax relief and not counted; with it, public would be about 17 percent. What is counted: Canada Council operating grant 305,000, Community Services Recovery Fund 50,000, other federal 35,638, BC Arts Council 99,000, BC Community Gaming 66,053, other provincial 2,900, North Vancouver Recreation and Culture Commission 200,000, other municipal 5,000. Private is memberships, donations and sponsorships 1,131,480 plus fundraising events 489,560; sponsorship is not separate. Earned revenues 2,207,719 are mainly shop, bookstore and venue rentals. Other revenue is in none of the three: amortization of deferred capital contributions 388,402, bank interest and endowment income 207,906, other 52,110. Expenses 5,408,624 gave an excess of 2,757. Net assets 567,742 exclude the endowment fund held by the Vancouver Foundation, which stood at 4,575,485 at market value at year end (note 11) after capital contributions of 1,419,458 during the year.

Musée national des beaux-arts du Québec.n: Musée national des beaux-arts du Québec
Musée national des beaux-arts du Québec.basis: Rapport de gestion 2023-2024, états financiers audited by the Auditor General of Quebec: État des résultats (p. 103, year to 31 March 2024), État de l'évolution de l'actif net (p. 104), auditor's report.
Musée national des beaux-arts du Québec.line: FY2023-24 revenue CAD 34.1M: about 75 percent Quebec and federal grants, 5 percent Foundation and sponsors, 8 percent donated art, 9 percent earned (audited statements, report p. 103).
Musée national des beaux-arts du Québec.note: Public is Quebec grants 24,454,620 (operations 18,203,585, capital 6,251,035) plus Canada 1,261,235. 'Autres subventions ou contributions' of 513,106 (500,000 in operations) is not attributed to a funder in the statements, so it is not counted. Private is Commandites 229,332 plus contributions from the museum's Foundation 1,424,616. Donated collection items 2,618,320 are booked as income and again as expense (acquisitions 2,704,070) and are in none of the three. Earned is tickets and memberships 1,504,420, parking 267,944, shop 708,766, food-service royalties 157,836, space rental 289,074, art and exhibition loans 129,741, education 127,155. Investment income 437,834 and other 18,458 are in none. Charges 34,406,937 gave a deficit of 264,480 (2022-23: 3,105,078). Net assets 6,653,278 are the operations fund (net debt 2,226,825), capital fund 7,130,024 and endowment fund 1,750,079.

MacKenzie Art Gallery.basis: Annual report 2024-25: Summary Statement of Revenues and Expenses (printed p. 49, year to 31 March 2025) and Summary Statement of Financial Position (printed p. 48); auditor's report on the summary statements.
MacKenzie Art Gallery.line: FY2024-25 revenue CAD 5.8M: about 22 percent operating grants, 7 percent programming grants, 49 percent fundraising, 16 percent earned (summary statements, annual report p. 49).
MacKenzie Art Gallery.note: Summary statements derived from audited statements; the full audited statements were not opened. Public is operating grants 1,283,600 only. Programming grants 432,793 are not attributed to funders in the summary, so they are not counted as public. Private is Fundraising Income 2,859,556 (donations, memberships, sponsorship and events together). The corporate sponsor list gives bands, not amounts, so sponsorship is null. Other income 292,283 is in none. Expenses 5,504,159 gave an excess of 323,416 (prior year a deficit of 362,847). Net assets 4,585,132 are 4,566,896 internally restricted and 18,236 unrestricted.

Museo de Arte Contemporáneo de Santiago.n: Museo de Arte Contemporáneo de Santiago
Museo de Arte Contemporáneo de Santiago.basis: Universidad de Chile, Decreto Universitario 101 of 24 January 2025 approving the 2025 budget of income and expenses (4 pages, thousands of pesos), published on the university's transparency page.
Museo de Arte Contemporáneo de Santiago.line: No separate accounts for the museum; its parent, Universidad de Chile, approved a 2025 budget of CLP 953.9bn, with CLP 43.6bn of direct state funding.
Museo de Arte Contemporáneo de Santiago.note: Figures are null: the museum belongs to the Faculty of Arts and has no budget line of its own in the university's published budget, and the university's actual accounts were not opened. Parent budget (approved, not actual), thousands of pesos: total income 953,860,710 equal to total spending; operating income 545,173,276 (sales of goods and services 279,896,374, tuition 258,448,077); transfers 84,700,119 (from public bodies 83,448,291, from private sector 1,251,828); direct state contribution (aporte fiscal directo) 43,617,280; borrowing 54,000,000. The 2025 budget is the latest on the page apart from 2026.

Hubei Museum of Art.basis: Hubei Department of Culture and Tourism budget disclosure page lists '湖北美术馆2026年度单位预算信息公开目录' (unit code 2026221052), which links to the provincial budget portal czt.hubei.gov.cn/budget.
Hubei Museum of Art.line: The museum files its own 2026 unit budget, but the provincial portal that holds it refused the request, so no figures were read.
Hubei Museum of Art.note: Figures are null: the unit budget sits in a single-page application on czt.hubei.gov.cn, and the request returned HTTP 412 with a page saying it was blocked as a security threat. I did not try to get past the block. The department's page confirms that the museum has its own unit budget for 2026 and lists final accounts for 2024 only for the department, the cultural relics centre and the provincial museum.

Museo de Arte y Diseño Contemporáneo.n: Museo de Arte y Diseño Contemporáneo
Museo de Arte y Diseño Contemporáneo.basis: Estado de liquidación presupuestaria 2019 (PDF embedded on the museum's site, last row 'Total egresos'): ordinary budget, modified budget, accrued expenditure for the period.
Museo de Arte y Diseño Contemporáneo.line: FY2019 spending CRC 292M against a national-budget allocation of CRC 345M, modified to CRC 348M; no income statement could be opened (budget execution 2019).
Museo de Arte y Diseño Contemporáneo.note: The museum's site posts budget execution only up to 2019 (the pin text says budgets to 2020; the 2020 statements page returned not found). The statement is expenditure only: ordinary budget 345,490,000.00, modified budget 347,634,055.18, total expenditure 292,289,659.58, available 55,344,395.59. The ordinary budget is the museum's appropriation in the national budget through the Ministry of Culture, but the document does not name the funding source, so public and income are null. The embedded income statement (Estado de rendimiento financiero 2019) returned not found when downloaded, so no revenue or net assets were read. Remuneration was 230,629,170.71 of the spending. No later years are published.

DOX Centre for Contemporary Art.basis: DOX Prague, a.s. (IČO 27177718) annual report 2025 filed in the Czech commercial register (sbírka listin): Finanční přehled, výsledovka and přijaté provozní dotace (PDF p. 96, thousands of CZK); Rozvaha, Pasiva line 083 Vlastní kapitál (PDF p. 104); auditor's report by Jonák Audit s.r.o. in the same file.
DOX Centre for Contemporary Art.line: FY2025 income CZK 74M: about 19 percent public grants, 20 percent foundations and supporters, 60 percent own earned income (annual report 2025 with audited accounts, p. 96).
DOX Centre for Contemporary Art.note: Figures are in thousands of crowns, converted. Public is operating grants from the City of Prague 10,350, Ministry of Culture 3,920, Prague 7 district 84 and State Culture Fund 70. Private is Nadační fond DOX 11,000, Nadační fond ABAKUS 1,000 (two foundations tied to the founders) and 'Podporovatelé' (supporters, here treated as sponsorship) 2,600. Foreign contributors 17 are in none. Grants and gifts total 26,441, which matches the sum. Earned is 'výnosy z vlastní činnosti' 44,712 (tickets, rentals, shop, services). Other operating income 303 and financial income 5 are in none. Costs 82,694 gave a loss of 8,633. Net assets are equity of 66,231 (2024: 74,864). The 2025 filing is the latest in the register; the DOX site posts annual reports only up to 2016.

Centro de Arte Contemporáneo de Quito.n: Centro de Arte Contemporáneo de Quito
Centro de Arte Contemporáneo de Quito.basis: Fundación Museos de la Ciudad, Cédula de gastos (institutional budget), period 01/2025 to 12/2025, programme 01 Quito cultura y patrimonio, project 009 Agenda cultural Centro de Arte Contemporáneo, published with its 2025 rendición de cuentas.
Centro de Arte Contemporáneo de Quito.line: No separate accounts for the centre; its parent foundation closed 2025 with a coded budget of USD 7.81M and USD 6.88M accrued spending, with no income side published.
Centro de Arte Contemporáneo de Quito.note: Figures are null because the centre has no accounts of its own and the file is an expenditure budget with no income or funding-source lines. Parent totals for the Fundación Museos de la Ciudad, 2025: initial allocation 6,795,000.00, reforms 1,018,512.19, coded 7,813,512.19, accrued (devengado) 6,876,987.88. The centre's own project line, Agenda cultural Centro de Arte Contemporáneo, has coded 243,797.70 and accrued 232,985.93, but staff (project 013, accrued 4,311,522.90) and operations (project 017, accrued 1,509,982.32) are budgeted for the whole foundation, so that line is not the centre's full cost. The pin text says the foundation acts on commission of the Quito municipality; no transfer figure was found in this file. No financial statements or income report was found on the rendición de cuentas page.

Crac Occitanie.basis: Région Occitanie, Rapport de présentation du Budget Primitif 2026, section III.5.3 'Les recettes du secteur culturel' (p. 30) and the culture orientation text (p. 71).
Crac Occitanie.line: No separate accounts for the Crac; the Région expects EUR 0.5M of income in 2026 from its four regional museums together, including tickets, grants and state funds (Budget Primitif 2026).
Crac Occitanie.note: Figures are null: the Crac is run directly by the Région as a service, so it has no accounts of its own, and the 2026 budget report gives only one combined revenue figure of 0.5 million euros for the Crac in Sète, the Sérignan museum, the Musée Cérès Franco and the Javols site, covering entry fees, grants and contributions from the state or other authorities. No line for the Crac's costs was found in the budget report, the Région's budget page or the Crac's own site. The Région's total 2026 budget was not itemised by site.

Museum Ludwig.basis: Stadt Köln Jahresabschluss 2023, Teil 2: Teilergebnisrechnung Produktgruppe 0402 Museum Ludwig (printed p. 178); Teil 3: Ergebnis Produktgruppe 0402 (printed pp. 110 to 111).
Museum Ludwig.line: FY2023 costs EUR 18.8M: about 75 percent City of Cologne general budget (net), 15 percent earned, 10 percent grants and allocations (Jahresabschluss 2023, Teilergebnisrechnung 0402).
Museum Ludwig.note: The museum is a department of the city with no separate accounts; these are the city's own actuals for product group 0402. Expenses (ordentliche Aufwendungen) are 18,794,339: personnel 3,831,230, goods and services 10,375,896, depreciation 3,683,341, transfers 35,684, other 868,188. Own revenue (ordentliche Erträge) is 4,791,020: grants and allocations 1,850,736 (funders not named, so not counted as public or private), private-law fees 2,761,673 (admissions, shop and similar), cost refunds 90,106, other 88,505. The ordinary result of minus 14,003,319 is carried by the city's general budget; income_total adds it to own revenue, so it equals expenses, and public is that figure. The printed Jahresergebnis is minus 14,521,202 after internal charges. 282,350 visitors, 39 percent non-paying. 2023 is the latest city accounts published. Ludwig Foundation and Friends' support named in the pin text is not itemised.

Lenbachhaus.basis: Haushaltsplan der Landeshauptstadt München 2026, Kulturreferat: Produktübersicht (printed p. 681, Ergebnis 2024) and Produkt 36252200 Städtische Galerie im Lenbachhaus und Kunstbau, Erträge und Aufwendungen (printed p. 701, Ergebnis 2024).
Lenbachhaus.line: FY2024 costs EUR 15.0M: about 77 percent City of Munich general budget (net), 20 percent admission and other fees, 3 percent grants from other bodies (Haushaltsplan 2026, product 36252200).
Lenbachhaus.note: The museum is a department of the city's Kulturreferat with no separate accounts; these are the city's product-level actuals for 2024. Expenses are ordentliche Aufwendungen 14,982,593.35: personnel 3,394,751, pensions 321,878, goods and services 8,664,186, depreciation 1,426,994, transfers 12,220, other 1,162,564. Own revenue is 3,456,191.89: public-law fees (admission) 2,277,425, private-law fees 770,184, grants and allocations 378,765 (funder not named), release of special items 29,697, other 120. Income_total is own revenue plus the net result of 11,526,401.46 (Ergebnis laufende Verwaltung), which the city's general budget carries, so it equals expenses; public is that net result. The grants of 378,765 are not counted as public or private because the plan does not name the funders (the pin text names Beisheim Stiftung, Pro Helvetia, Art Mentor Foundation and Herbert Schuchardt-Stiftung as 2025 donors). Earned is the two fee lines. Visitors 370,924 in 2024. The plan for 2025 and 2026 sets own revenue at 2,450,127 and expenses at 14,430,470 and 16,052,802. Net assets are not given for the unit.

Kunsthalle Münster.basis: Stadt Münster Jahresabschluss 2024, Band 2: Produktgruppe 0401 Kulturamt, Teilergebnisrechnung (printed p. 205); the Kunsthalle appears only in the text of product 040102 Kulturveranstaltungen und -preise (p. 203).
Kunsthalle Münster.line: No separate accounts for the Kunsthalle; the city's Kulturamt group closed 2024 with EUR 0.92M revenue and EUR 6.66M expenses (Jahresabschluss 2024, p. 205).
Kunsthalle Münster.note: Figures are null: the Kunsthalle has no product or cost-centre line of its own in the city's 2024 accounts; it is named only in the text of product 040102 (cultural events and prizes) inside the Kulturamt group. Parent totals for Produktgruppe 0401 Kulturamt, 2024: grants and allocations 599,381.50, private-law fees 170,443.55, cost refunds 152,006.70, other 2,518.50, total ordinary revenue 924,350.25; ordinary expenses 6,663,399.22 (personnel 1,517,517.75, transfers 3,913,676.05, other 903,725.06); ordinary result minus 5,739,048.97 and minus 7,595,588.97 after internal charges; expense coverage 10.9 percent. These totals cover culture funding, festivals, public art and district culture as well as the Kunsthalle, so none of it is the Kunsthalle's own budget.

Haus für Medienkunst Oldenburg.basis: Stadt Oldenburg Jahresabschluss 2022 (398 pages): Teilhaushalt 06 Kultur, Museen, Sport, Teil-Ergebnisrechnung (JA 79); list of earmarked carry-overs for product P10.252001 Kulturgutvermittlung; Bilanz Edith-Ruß-Stiftung (JA 245 to 246).
Haus für Medienkunst Oldenburg.line: No separate accounts for the house; the city's culture, museums and sport sub-budget closed 2022 with EUR 2.39M revenue and EUR 32.6M expenses (Jahresabschluss 2022).
Haus für Medienkunst Oldenburg.note: Figures are null: the city's 2022 accounts have no line for the Haus für Medienkunst (formerly the Edith-Russ-Haus); it sits in product P10.252001 Kulturgutvermittlung with the city museums, and only an earmarked carry-over of 17,495.01 is named for it. Parent totals, Teilhaushalt 06 Kultur, Museen, Sport, 2022: ordinary revenue 2,393,434.65 (grants and allocations 540,552.64, public-law fees 436,984.68, private-law fees 994,595.55, other 352,779.16), ordinary expenses 32,582,237.73 (personnel 8,401,765.24, transfers 11,923,786.39). The Edith-Ruß-Stiftung, a separate city foundation named after the donor, shows a net position of 1,079,281.14 at the end of 2022, held as loans, and so produces almost no income. The 2022 city accounts were the latest the pin's checker found; a later year was not searched for. The pin's Stiftung Niedersachsen grants of EUR 12,500 are not in these accounts.

Kunsthalle Recklinghausen.basis: City of Recklinghausen Jahresabschluss PDF named in the pin sources; the city's site failed the certificate check, so it was not opened.
Kunsthalle Recklinghausen.line: No figures: the City of Recklinghausen's website failed the security certificate check, and no other copy of the city accounts or a Kunsthalle budget line was found.
Kunsthalle Recklinghausen.note: Figures are null: both recklinghausen.de and the named Jahresabschluss PDF failed TLS certificate verification (curl error 60), and I did not turn verification off. One web search for a Kunsthalle product line in the city budget returned only the Kreis Recklinghausen budget and a 2016 culture department presentation, neither with a Kunsthalle figure. The Kunsthalle is run by the city's museums department, so it probably has no separate accounts even if the city accounts could be read.

Reykjavík Art Museum.basis: Ársskýrsla 2023 (annual report 2023 of Listasafn Reykjavíkur), 'Fjármál og rekstur' and key figures, p. 11: own income, City of Reykjavik contribution, income split, costs (figures in thousands of krónur).
Reykjavík Art Museum.line: FY2023 income ISK 704M: about 77 percent City of Reykjavik contribution, 23 percent own income, mostly tickets and shop (annual report 2023, p. 11).
Reykjavík Art Museum.note: The museum is a department of the City of Reykjavik, so there are no separate audited accounts; these are the annual report's own figures. Income total is own income 160,798,000 plus the City contribution 543,621,000, which equals total costs: salaries 300,787,000, internal rent 191,065,000 (a charge from the city, not an outside cost), other operating costs 212,567,000. Own income splits into tickets 46 percent, shop 25 percent, grants 16 percent, venue hire 9 percent, other 5 percent; the amounts are not printed, so earned, private and sponsorship are null, and the source of the grants is not named. Net assets are not stated. 2023 is the latest annual report on the museum's site.

VISUAL.basis: VISUAL's governance page links the 2024 financial statements of Carlow Arts Centre Ltd on a SharePoint site; the link returned HTTP 403.
VISUAL.line: The 2024 financial statements of Carlow Arts Centre Ltd are linked from VISUAL's site, but the link refused access, so no figures were read.
VISUAL.note: Figures are null: the statements link (carlowartscentre.sharepoint.com) answered 403 Forbidden to a plain request, and I did not try to get past it. The company's filings at the Companies Registration Office are sold, not open, and a search found no copy elsewhere (a result for Carlow Arts Festival is a different company). The governance page says VISUAL is a project of Carlow Arts Centre Ltd, a company limited by shares whose shareholder is Carlow County Council, and thanks Carlow County Council, the Arts Council, the Department of Tourism, Culture, Arts, Gaeltacht, Sport and Media, Creative Ireland, the Heritage Council, Carlow College and Carlow LEO.

Crawford Art Gallery.basis: Crawford Art Gallery Cork financial statements for the year ended 31 December 2024, certified by the Comptroller and Auditor General: Statement of Financial Activities (p. 29), note 2a to 2d (pp. 40 to 41), Balance Sheet (p. 31).
Crawford Art Gallery.line: FY2024 income EUR 3.85M: about 91 percent Department of Culture grants (30 percent capital), 1 percent donations and sponsorship, 1 percent earned (audited statements, p. 29).
Crawford Art Gallery.note: Calendar year 2024; the gallery closed to the public in late September 2024 for redevelopment. The text layer of the PDF is a poor scan, so numbers were checked against the statement totals. Public is Oireachtas grants 3,502,541 from Vote 33: current 2,292,000, capital 162,000, additional capital 991,274 (2023: 2,661,914), centenary 57,267. Capital grants make up about 30 percent of income. Private is public donations 15,303 plus sponsorship 16,485. Donated artworks 90,600 are non-cash and not counted. Earned is gallery shop profit 8,728 (sales 22,217 less costs), rental 14,040 and education 15,005; a VAT rebate of 6,847 is left out. Deferred funding for retirement benefits 181,000 and bank interest 843 are in none. Expenditure 2,974,860 gave net income of 876,532 before capital transfers. Net assets 45,211,771 are mostly heritage artworks 37,593,136 and buildings.

Castello di Rivoli.basis: Bilancio consuntivo (rendiconto) 31 December 2025: rendiconto gestionale proventi p. 7, income detail pp. 24 to 25, stato patrimoniale p. 4 (patrimonio netto).
Castello di Rivoli.line: FY2025 income EUR 5.0M: about 57 percent public grants (Regione Piemonte, Turin, Rivoli, ministry), 28 percent private (foundations, patrons, friends), 14 percent earned (rendiconto p. 7).
Castello di Rivoli.note: Italian rendiconto read from the PDF text; legal audit is by the Collegio dei Revisori. Public is line 1 of institutional income, 2,842,120: Regione Piemonte 2,489,000 (founding-member fee 510,000 plus institutional grant 1,979,000), City of Turin 75,000, Rivoli 15,000, ministry of culture (Italian Council, PAC) 225,620, Rivoli and Rivalta education 37,500. Private is 1,133,856 from private bodies (Compagnia di San Paolo, Fondazione CRT, Intesa, Art Bonus gifts 42,500, friends and others) plus 260,650 from non-members (benefactor, supporter and friend fees 139,500, gifts 121,150). Bank foundations are counted as private. Intesa lunch talks 26,667 is the only line named as a partner payment; no line is labelled sponsorship, so sponsorship is null. Earned is ticket sales 202,752 (including Fondazione Cerruti), department activities 112,259 and accessory income 389,110 (hall rental, cafe, bookshop, Cerruti). In none of the three: financial income 2,074 and other income 64,887 (prior-year gains, release of funds). Net result is zero. The pin text cites 2023 income EUR 5.6M; 2024 income was 5,107,865.

Fondazione Sandretto Re Rebaudengo.basis: Bilancio Sociale 2025, situazione economico finanziaria: stato patrimoniale p. 20, rendiconto economico and split of public and private contributions p. 21.
Fondazione Sandretto Re Rebaudengo.line: FY2025 income EUR 2.94M: about 73 percent private contributions, 13 percent public contributions, 12 percent earned (bilancio sociale 2025, p. 21).
Fondazione Sandretto Re Rebaudengo.note: The social report reproduces the foundation's balance sheet and profit and loss; the auditor's report was not read. Revenue total 2,938,761 is sales and services 181,983, change in inventories 52,284, operating contributions 2,541,165 and other income 163,329. The report splits the operating contributions into public 384,020 and private 2,157,145 without naming payers, so partners such as Regione Piemonte, Fondazione CRT, Compagnia di San Paolo and Asja cannot be assigned. Earned is sales and services plus other income; the inventory change is in none of the three. No line is labelled sponsorship, so sponsorship is null. Net assets are the equity total 1,667,135. Costs 2,865,572; result for the year 3,958 after finance costs and tax.

Aomori Museum of Art.basis: Aomori Museum of Art annual report FY2023 (Reiwa 5), p. 84 shaded table 'Operating budget and settlement', general account outturn, thousand yen.
Aomori Museum of Art.line: FY2023 outturn JPY 883.5M: about 84 percent prefectural funds (481M general revenue, 131M bonds, 131M fund transfers), 8 percent fees and charges (annual report p. 84).
Aomori Museum of Art.note: Prefecture-run museum with no separate accounts: the table is the Aomori Prefecture general-account line for the museum, in thousand yen. Income: general revenue 481,353, prefectural bonds 131,000, transfers from funds 130,816, fees and charges 69,854, miscellaneous income 70,434, property income 48, national treasury 0. Public is the first three, all prefectural resources, and includes 131,000 of borrowing and 130,816 of fund transfers. Earned is fees and charges, which are admissions and facility use. Miscellaneous income 70,434 and property income 48 are in none of the three because the report does not say what they hold. Spending 883,505: staff 149,814, museum operation 732,988, park management 703. The budget was 863,498. The Supportship donor club keeps its own accounts, which are not included. A later annual report was not on the museum's site.

Pola Museum of Art.basis: Pola Art Foundation statement of changes in net assets, 1 April 2025 to 31 March 2026, one page: ordinary revenue and expense, section III net assets.
Pola Museum of Art.line: FY2025 income JPY 4.93B: about 83 percent endowment dividends, 16 percent earned museum revenue, 1 percent other; no grant or donation line (net-assets statement).
Pola Museum of Art.note: Figures are for the Pola Art Foundation as a whole, which runs the museum and its research and artist support; the museum has no separate accounts on the foundation's site. Ordinary revenue: income from basic assets (the endowment) 4,089,488,094, income from designated assets 9,544,920, project revenue 793,273,975, miscellaneous 38,421,642. Project revenue is the earned figure (museum admissions and related services). The statement has no subsidy, grant or donation line, so public and private are null rather than zero because the miscellaneous line is not itemised. Expenses 1,543,998,618: projects 1,495,502,426, administration 48,496,192. Valuation gain on basic assets 2,751,593,040 is outside ordinary revenue and excluded. Net assets 189,746,038,027 at 31 March 2026 (designated 136,500,574,430). The foundation's balance sheet and business report for the year were also opened.

Sapporo International Art Festival.source_kind: executive committee settlement published by the City of Sapporo
Sapporo International Art Festival.basis: SIAF Executive Committee income and expenditure settlement FY2023 (Reiwa 5), one page: income lines 1 to 4, expenditure lines 1 to 7.
Sapporo International Art Festival.line: FY2023 festival-year income JPY 570M: about 84 percent City of Sapporo contribution, 4 percent sponsors, 6 percent tickets, 6 percent other (executive committee settlement).
Sapporo International Art Festival.note: The festival organiser is the SIAF Executive Committee, run by the City of Sapporo. FY2023 (April 2023 to March 2024) is the festival year with artwork production 247,974,392 and venue costs 116,117,906, so it was used instead of FY2024. FY2024 read too: income 88,630,411 (City 54,991,000, other 33,639,411, no sponsors or tickets) and spending 66,901,672. Income lines FY2023: City contribution 479,310,600, sponsorship 23,611,514, tickets and similar 34,861,835, other 31,792,762. The settlement does not itemise other income, so no national or foundation grant is counted as public or private.
