Henry Moore Institute.basis: Henry Moore Foundation (charity 271370) trustees' report and consolidated accounts to 31 March 2025: SOFA p. 33, note 3 p. 36 (Contributions from Leeds City Council), financial review p. 21.
Henry Moore Institute.line: The Institute has no accounts of its own; its parent Foundation reports FY2024-25 income GBP 8.0M, and Leeds City Council gives the Institute GBP 145,743.
Henry Moore Institute.note: The Institute is a programme of the Henry Moore Foundation and publishes no accounts of its own, so income, expenditure and shares are null. Public 145,743 is the Leeds City Council contribution to the Institute's running costs, stated in note 3 (same in 2024). Parent figures for 2024-25: total income 7,958,098 (investments 2,979,496; sale of cultural assets 4,043,237 plus 47,286 in the trading subsidiary; other trading 163,149; Museum and Gallery Tax Relief 158,375; charitable income 531,555 including admissions 227,225; donations and grants 35,000 of which Stonewater 15,000 and Yorkshire Sculpture International partners 20,000); total expenditure 6,136,979; net assets 129,052,551. The Foundation approved grants of 569,000. Arts Council England funds the Yorkshire Sculpture International partnership only, as bridge funding, with no amount stated.

Kramskoi Voronezh Regional Art Museum.basis: Godovoj otchet 2024, section Khozyaystvennaya deyatelnost (page 4): total receipts, income from statutory activity, spending.
Kramskoi Voronezh Regional Art Museum.line: FY2024 receipts RUB 69.6M, of which RUB 12.5M, about 18 percent, is the museum's own income from paid activity; the report does not itemise the rest.
Kramskoi Voronezh Regional Art Museum.note: The annual report states: receipts 69,596 thousand roubles, of which income from statutory (paid) activity 12,537 thousand; spending 62,674 thousand, of which 5,051 thousand on exhibitions. The remaining 57,059 thousand is not labelled; as a state budgetary institution of Voronezh Oblast it is state-assignment and other budget subsidy, but the report does not say so, so public is left null. The museum's plan of financial and economic activity for 2024 (a plan, not actuals) shows income of 58,696,810 roubles with a state-assignment subsidy of 39,886,803. The register bo.nalog.gov.ru did not return the museum, as budget institutions report through the Treasury. A 100,000 rouble VK advertising grant was received in Q4 2023.

Ural Industrial Biennial of Contemporary.n: Ural Industrial Biennial of Contemporary Art
Ural Industrial Biennial of Contemporary.line: No figure read: the biennial is run by the Ural branch of the Pushkin Museum's National Centre for Contemporary Arts and has no accounts of its own.
Ural Industrial Biennial of Contemporary.note: The biennial has no separate legal entity or accounts; it is a programme of the Ural branch of the National Centre for Contemporary Arts, part of the Pushkin State Museum of Fine Arts since 2020, whose statements are published on pushkinmuseum.art. That site's TLS certificate chain failed verification from this machine (self-signed certificate in chain, the Russian national certificate authority), so the museum's activity-results page was not opened and no parent totals were read. The only figure available is the pin text's budget of about 100 million roubles for the 6th edition (2021), which is a project budget from a secondary source and not entered. The register bo.nalog.gov.ru and bus.gov.ru were not searched further for this unit.

Yekaterinburg Museum of Fine Arts.basis: Form 0503721 Otchet o finansovykh rezultatakh deyatelnosti uchrezhdeniya at 1 January 2025 (MAUK Yekaterinburg Museum of Fine Arts, INN 6661004252), pp. 1-3: lines 010-110 and 150, columns for targeted funds, state assignment and income-generating activity.
Yekaterinburg Museum of Fine Arts.line: FY2024 income RUB 249.5M: about 79 percent city assignment and targeted subsidies, 1 percent private gifts, 19 percent own paid services and rent; expenditure RUB 273.4M (Form 0503721).
Yekaterinburg Museum of Fine Arts.note: Public 196,934,900 is the municipal-assignment amount 159,400,000 (booked on the paid-services line 131 in the state-assignment column, paid through the city culture department that founded the museum) plus targeted funds 37,534,900 from the public sector (line 152). Private 2,500,000 is a cash gift from non-government residents (line 155); non-cash gifts of 2,441,807 (organisations 1,632,000 and 383,325, individuals 3,165, other 419,758) and 457,719 from public bodies sit in neither field. Earned 48,369,537 is paid services 48,261,003 plus rent 108,534. Neither field: cost compensation 98,896, conditional lease income 22,541, social insurance refunds 40,384, fines 12,747, asset disposal result -1,337,632. Total income 249,537,339.99 is the form's line 010. Expenditure 273,357,538.12 (line 150) is higher than income, mostly depreciation and non-cash costs; no balance sheet was read, so net assets are null. A municipal autonomous institution founded by the Department of Culture of Yekaterinburg administration.

NTU Centre for Contemporary Art Singapor.n: NTU Centre for Contemporary Art Singapore
NTU Centre for Contemporary Art Singapor.line: No accounts found: the centre is a unit of Nanyang Technological University with no published budget; its site names NTU and the Economic Development Board as co-funders.
NTU Centre for Contemporary Art Singapor.note: NTU CCA Singapore is a research centre of Nanyang Technological University, co-funded by NTU and the Singapore Economic Development Board per the pin's source, and no financial statement, annual report or budget for the centre is published on ntu.ccasingapore.org (the about page lists governing council members from NTU, EDB and the National Arts Council but no figures). NTU's own annual reports page links reports only up to 2019, and its revenue facts page gives no totals as text, so no parent total was read. All figures are null.

Singapore Art Museum.basis: Audited annual report (Deloitte) for the year ended 31 March 2026: statement of comprehensive income p. 26, balance sheet p. 27, note 4 p. 38, accounting policy 2.9 p. 36, note 20 p. 44 of the financial statements.
Singapore Art Museum.line: FY2025-26 income SGD 35.5M: about 61 percent government grants, 13 percent donations, 24 percent other grants, 1 percent earned (audited statements p. 26, Singapore Biennale year).
Singapore Art Museum.note: Total income 35,523,916 is income 5,084,363 plus grants 30,439,553. Public 21,763,016 is operating grants 20,450,945 plus deferred capital grants amortised 1,312,071; policy 2.9 defines both as government grants, and note 21 says the museum is mainly funded by government grants, without naming the ministry. Private 4,650,561 is donation income: cash 3,383,390 and in-kind 1,267,171 (note 4). Other grants 8,676,537 name no funder and sit in neither field (the notes do not name their funders, and the Tote Board matching grant is not itemised). Earned 433,802 is admission fees 147,319, service income 57,431 and other income 229,052. The year includes Singapore Biennale 2025 (exhibition expenses 10.8M against 7.1M the year before), which lifts both donations (2025: 800,025) and other grants (2025: 5,003,981). Net assets 5,676,126. Income in the year to 31 March 2025 was 26,405,276.

Moderna galerija.basis: Letno porocilo 2024, Racunovodsko porocilo: accrual income statement p. 56-57 (AOP 870, 887, 888), balance sheet p. 55 (AOP 044), cash-basis statement pp. 57-58 (AOP 401-430) for the split by source.
Moderna galerija.line: FY2024 income EUR 2.69M; on the cash statement of EUR 2.64M, about 91 percent is state budget and EU funds, 8 percent other non-tax revenue (annual report pp. 57-58).
Moderna galerija.note: Income 2,688,353 and expenditure 2,612,833 are the accrual figures (surplus 75,519). The split by source exists only on the cash-basis statement, total receipts 2,635,932: state budget 2,390,387 (current spending 2,323,687, investment 66,700), EU institutions and other states 20,400, other non-tax revenue 208,237, interest 11,908, domestic donations 5,000; so shares are about the cash total. Public is the state budget plus EU funds, 2,410,787. Earned is other non-tax revenue (tickets, sales, rentals) 208,237; interest sits in neither field. Net assets is the balance sheet line own funds and long-term liabilities 27,792,118, mostly liabilities to fund fixed assets 25,882,157 and long-term deferred items 1,813,802. The museum is a public institute of the Ministry of Culture. The earlier ministry note of 2.07M for the 2022 programme is a different year.

Wits Art Museum.basis: No separate accounts for the museum. Parent: University of the Witwatersrand, Annual Integrated Report 2025, group financial highlights (printed p. 103-105 of the PDF).
Wits Art Museum.line: Wits Art Museum has no accounts of its own; its parent Wits Group reports 2025 income ZAR 13.06bn, of which state subsidies and grants are ZAR 2.88bn, about 22 percent.
Wits Art Museum.note: WAM is a unit of the University of the Witwatersrand, so every figure is null. Parent group, calendar 2025 (rand millions): total income 13,061; state subsidies and grants 2,881; tuition and other fees 3,144; research contracts 3,243; other income 2,239 (restricted external income 1,580); interest, dividends and exchange gains 560; expenditure 11,514; surplus for the year 1,430. The Standard Bank collection partnership and the early donors in the pin text are not itemised in the group accounts. The document was read in a browser because the university's web server sends an incomplete certificate chain that command-line tools reject.

Busan Biennale.line: No accounts found: the Busan Biennale Organizing Committee, an incorporated association, publishes no budget or settlement on its site.
Busan Biennale.note: The organiser is the Busan Biennale Organizing Committee (an incorporated association, tax number 607-82-08717) acting for Busan Metropolitan City. Its site (pages on sponsorship and organisation, 2022 and 2025 editions) carries a sponsor-recruitment page and no financial statement, and no budget line was reached in the city's finance pages. Disclosure for such associations sits on the national tax service's public-interest corporation portal, a script-driven application that was not opened. Two web searches for the 2024 total budget returned only news items without figures. The funders in the pin text (BNK Busan Bank, Shinsegae, Naver, foreign cultural funds) are sponsors and cannot be placed without amounts. All figures are null.

Changwon Sculpture Biennale.basis: No separate accounts for the biennale. Parent: Changwon Cultural Foundation 2025 settlement (2025 fiscal-year closing report, local public-investment-institution standard): statement of operating results p. 25-26, net assets statement p. 27.
Changwon Sculpture Biennale.line: The biennale has no accounts of its own; its host Changwon Cultural Foundation reports 2025 income KRW 19.8bn, of which KRW 15.3bn, about 77 percent, is city contributions.
Changwon Sculpture Biennale.note: The biennale is a project of Changwon Cultural Foundation (a public foundation of Changwon City) and the 2025 settlement lists no biennale budget; 2025 is a gap year between the 2024 and 2026 editions, and the settlement only shows a 61,434,000 won refund of 2024 biennale grants owed to Gyeongnam Province and 23,500,000 won of prologue costs for 2026. All figures are null. Parent, 2025, won: operating income 19,816,614,119 = city contributions 15,265,111,067, subsidies 802,738,770, donations 35,000,000, admissions 1,055,475,973, hall rentals 813,918,935, leases 114,760,041, agency projects 1,181,667,347, incidental 304,074,970, parking 149,914,844, other 93,952,172; operating costs 19,182,355,785; net income 874,805,638; net assets 1,116,525,249. The 2024 comparison income was 19,112,468,714.

Amorepacific Museum of Art.line: The museum is run directly by Amorepacific Corp and has no accounts of its own; the company's audit-report page returned a block to this machine, so no figure was read.
Amorepacific Museum of Art.note: Corporate museum with no separate legal entity, so there is no public or private split to read; its funding is the parent company's money (neither public nor private by this scheme). The company's audit-reports page at apgroup.com answered HTTP 403 to plain requests and was not pursued, per the rule against getting past blocks. All figures are null.

Arko Art Center.basis: No separate accounts for the art centre. Parent: Arts Council Korea Sustainability Management Report 2025 (2024 data), ESG Factbook, Financial Performance, fund account summary statement of financial position.
Arko Art Center.line: Arko Art Center has no accounts of its own; its parent Arts Council Korea reports KRW 754.5bn net assets for 2024 and no income statement.
Arko Art Center.note: The art centre is one of the Arts Council Korea facilities (with the Arts Theater, Daehakro Arts Theater and House of Artists), so every figure is null. Parent fund account at end of 2024, KRW million: total assets 839,105; total liabilities 84,592; total net assets 754,512. The report prints a balance-sheet summary only; it has no revenue or budget table, so no income or public share was read (ALIO, the public-institution disclosure site, was not opened). The report states about KRW 425.2 billion donated through ARKO over 50 years and total sponsorship of about KRW 1.2 billion linked in the year. Funding is public by status: the council is a national body.

Fundació Antoni Tàpies.basis: Comptes anuals abreujats 2024 with auditor's report (Busquet, 23 May 2025): compte de resultats abreujat lines 1, 6, 7-9, 10, 13 (pp. 12-13 of the PDF); balanc abreujat, patrimoni net (p. 10); grants by funder from Subvencions 2021-2025 table on the transparency page.
Fundació Antoni Tàpies.line: FY2024 activity income EUR 2.87M: about 69 percent public grants, 6 percent donations and sponsors, 26 percent earned (audited accounts 2024, lines 1 and 6).
Fundació Antoni Tàpies.note: Income 2,868,281 is income from activities (line 1, 2,639,115) plus other activity income (line 6, 229,166, mostly rentals 194,796); it leaves out capital grants released to the result 431,335, other results 78,027 and financial income 2,093. Expenditure 3,240,389 is operating costs: supplies 686,201, staff 1,123,242, other operating 913,461, depreciation 482,914, grants awarded 34,570. Public 1,971,646 is official grants to activities (line 1d), which the foundation's grants table splits for 2024 into Generalitat 928,733, Barcelona City Council 407,056, Diputacio de Barcelona 150,000 and Ministerio de Cultura 478,920 and others. Private 184,123 is sponsors, promotion and collaborations 115,840 (also the sponsorship figure) plus donations 68,283. Earned 737,218 is sales and services 508,053, rentals 194,796 and other 34,370. A reimbursement of grants and donations of 24,707 sits in neither. The foundation's table shows 2025 grants of 2,757,406 (Ministry of Culture 1,171,079 including the capital-of-culture line). Net assets 55,264,020 are patrimoni net, of which 6,137,256 are capital grants and donations and the rest the endowment fund of 48,654,379 and reserves.

Fundació Joan Miró.basis: Comptes anuals 2025 with Grant Thornton audit report: compte de resultats 2025 (p. 9 of the PDF), balanc de situacio (p. 8), estat de canvis en el patrimoni net (p. 10-11).
Fundació Joan Miró.line: FY2025 income EUR 12.0M: about 31 percent official grants, 15 percent other grants, donations and sponsorship, 54 percent earned from tickets, shop, services and rentals (audited accounts, income statement).
Fundació Joan Miró.note: Income 11,989,781 is income from activities 10,845,841 plus other activity income 1,143,940. Public 3,695,610 is official grants to activities (Generalitat, Barcelona council and Ministry of Culture are on the board; the notes that split it by funder are not in the filed pages). Private 1,787,265 is other grants, donations and bequests recognised in the result; the line is not split between corporate sponsors (BBVA, la Caixa, Puig and others named in the pin text) and any non-official grants. Earned 6,506,906 is sales 2,498,303, services 2,864,663, rentals 502,110 and other 641,830. Neither field: capital grants released to the result 327,527 and other results 35,326. Expenditure 12,498,011 is operating costs: supplies 1,121,688, staff 4,402,392 (net of a 160,606 provision release), other operating 6,415,432 and depreciation 558,499; the year result is a deficit of 164,063 after financial costs. Net assets 33,558,235 (2024: 33,401,235) include the collection and building. The income statement was read from the OCR-quality scan and checks to the operating result of -145,377.

Museo Reina Sofía.basis: Cuentas anuales 2025 filed in the IGAE public accounts registry (Recuenta): XBRL cuenta del resultado economico-patrimonial and balance; Memoria 24302MEM12025A.pdf note 14.1 pp. 15-17 (transfers and sponsorship by name).
Museo Reina Sofía.line: FY2025 income EUR 42.6M excluding capital transfers: about 68 percent state transfers and EU, 3 percent named corporate and foundation gifts, 22 percent tickets and services (accounts 2025, note 14.1).
Museo Reina Sofía.note: Statutory ordinary income is 51,372,065 (the audit report is dated 10 July 2026). It includes capital transfers from the Ministry of Culture of 8,806,389, left out of income_total as a one-off for works; including them public would be 37,785,249. Public 28,978,860 is current transfers from the ministry 28,927,840 plus the Creative Europe grant 51,020. Private 1,463,000 is cash gifts named in note 14.1 on a budget-rights basis: la Caixa 300,000, Mutua Madrilena 300,000, Inditex 300,000, Mapfre 175,000, El Corte Ingles 150,000, Fundacion Damm 75,000, Damm SA 55,000 and others; the accounts' income statement shows 1,274,764 of subsidies to finance expenses after deferral, a different basis, so the fields are not strictly additive. Sponsorship 570,500 is the company gifts (Inditex, El Corte Ingles, Damm, Bimba y Lola, Illycaffe, Iberia, Sotheby's). Gifts in kind of 490,405 (including a public body, Adif, 176,972) are in neither field, as are Madrid city 65,000, INAP 25,716, a Banco de Espana agreement 40,000 (central bank, neither public nor private here), a Universitat Oberta de Catalunya teaching agreement 247,930 and other ordinary income 2,295,790. Earned 9,495,112 is public fees (tasas) 1,407,451 plus services 8,087,661. Expenditure 43,215,099 is ordinary expenses incl. staff 21,473,155 and depreciation 1,680,090. Net assets 595,658,949 are the state's building and collection.

Es Baluard Museu.basis: Fundacio Es Baluard Museu d'Art Contemporani de Palma, comptes anuals PIMESFL 2025 with audit report: compte de resultat p. 7, note 13 sector table p. 42-43, balanc p. 5-6.
Es Baluard Museu.line: FY2025 income EUR 3.27M: about 78 percent public (Govern, Consell de Mallorca, Palma, state), 3 percent private sponsors and grants, 19 percent earned (audited accounts, notes 13 and 15).
Es Baluard Museu.note: Income 3,265,868 is income from own activity 2,646,062 plus sales and other activity income 333,170 and 286,636; capital grants released to the result (416,632, Govern) and interest 4,646 are left out. Public 2,534,999.88 is Govern de les Illes Balears 870,000, Consell de Mallorca 840,000, Ajuntament de Palma 774,999.96 and the state 49,999.92. Private 111,062 is private-sector income of 86,062 (sponsors, promotions and user contributions of 4,780) plus a 25,000 operating grant that the sector table assigns to the private sector. Earned 619,806 is sales and other income 333,170 plus other activity income 286,636. Expenditure 3,756,963 is supplies 117,049, staff 980,885, other 2,223,152 and depreciation 435,877; the statutory result is a deficit of 69,816 after the capital grant release. Net assets 20,318,367 are mostly capital grants 18,228,210 (public 16,643,405) held against the building and collection.

Tabakalera.basis: Memoria 2025, section Gestión, 'Ejecución presupuestaria 2025' tables (printed pp. 64-65): Ingresos, Gastos de personal, Gasto corriente.
Tabakalera.line: FY2025 own income EUR 1.87M against spending of EUR 7.45M; the owners' contribution that covers the gap is not itemised in the report (memoria 2025, p. 64).
Tabakalera.note: Income_total is the report's 'Ingresos en total' 1,868,936.24 (execution): Gestión 1,010,340.30, Contenidos 479,085.89, Dpto. Desarrollo (neto) 348,678.49, Comunicación 831.56, Nominativos 30,000. It is own income only; the contribution from the public owners that funds the rest is not a line in the report. Expenditure_total is the sum of two printed totals: personnel 2,375,205.40 plus current spending 5,077,239.18. The printed 'Resultado total' row (5,209,550.52 against 5,250,000) repeats the 2024 report exactly and does not match the 2025 lines; 2025 spending less income from the printed lines is 5,583,508.34 (budget 5,620,000). The text says rental income and fees fund self-financing and that the Basque Government culture department paid nominal grants for the arts-science, film lab and Noka projects, above budget, without amounts, so public, private, sponsorship and earned are left null. The 2024 budget-execution page was also read: income 2,066,276.15 including nominal grants 270,000, spending 7,275,826.67, net 5,209,550.52. No audited accounts are published on the transparency page, only the memoria and a 2024 budget table.

Artium Museoa.source_kind: Basque foundations registry (Registro de Fundaciones del País Vasco, open data)
Artium Museoa.basis: Registry row F-98 Fundación Artium de Álava, FY2024: results file lines 1, 2, 7, 3, 4, 6, 8, 9 (cuenta de resultados); balance file row F-98, A) Patrimonio neto.
Artium Museoa.line: FY2024 operating income EUR 4.53M, of which EUR 4.40M is activity income (grants, donations, sponsorship; not split in the registry) and EUR 0.12M commercial sales.
Artium Museoa.note: Artium's own site (transparency page and the public grants PDF) is behind a human-verification check, so the foundation's accounts could not be opened; figures come from the Basque Government's open-data foundations registry, which carries the filed income statement. Income_total is line 1 'ingresos de la actividad propia' 4,401,595.20 (subsidies, donations, sponsorship and membership booked to the surplus) plus line 2 'ventas y otros ingresos de la actividad mercantil' 118,002.36 plus line 7 'otros ingresos de la actividad' 13,903.61. Excluded: capital subsidies released to the surplus 1,174,696.70 (offsets depreciation of the same size) and financial income 16,890.31. Expenditure_total is lines 3, 4, 6, 8, 9: aid paid 7,000, stock change 12,219.52, supplies 2,284.60, personnel 1,483,771.63, other activity costs 3,041,956.96; depreciation 1,174,696.70 excluded. Surplus from activity -13,731.54, with financial income 3,158.77 (balance file shows 3,102.49). The registry does not split line 1 between public grants and private money, so public and private are null. The pin text cites 2024 grants from the Diputación Foral de Álava (2.53M), Basque Government (1.72M), Ministry of Culture (150,000) and Vitoria-Gasteiz (130,000), which I could not check against the foundation's PDF. Net assets is patrimonio neto 54,593,233.05, of which 54,412,929.42 is capital subsidies, donations and bequests received (mostly the building fit-out and collection).

Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art Sr.n: Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art Sri Lanka
Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art Sr.basis: Financial statements to 31 March 2025 (EY Colombo, signed 26 Aug 2025): statement of income p. 3; note 3 incoming donations and note 4 other income p. 11; statement of financial position p. 4.
Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art Sr.line: FY2024-25 income LKR 102.7M: about 99.8 percent donations and sponsorship (founder patrons 27.2M, other sponsorship 75.2M); no government or earned income line (audited statements, pp. 3, 11).
Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art Sr.note: Scanned PDF, read from page images. Income is incoming resources 102,486,039 (founder patron donations 27,238,216 plus other sponsorship 75,247,823) plus other income 179,024 (exchange gain 173,064, write-off 5,960). The sponsorship line names no funders, so its mix of corporate, foundation and other non-government money is not stated; it is labelled sponsorship and counted as private. The statements show no government grant line, and public is left null because the sponsorship line is unnamed. Expenditure equals income, net surplus nil, because the accounting policy moves endowment-fund advances into income to match expenses. Founder Patrons advance towards endowment fund is a liability of 1,310,006 (7,343,310 a year earlier); reserves are nil, so net assets are shown as 0. Prior year: income 91,473,062, sponsorship 77,150,296, founder patrons 14,263,751.

Lunds Konsthall.basis: Lunds kommun årsredovisning 2025: Kultur- och fritidsnämnden, pp. 31-32 (cost base) and p. 101 (result); no line names Lunds Konsthall.
Lunds Konsthall.line: No separate accounts for Lunds Konsthall; the culture and leisure committee's 2025 cost base was just over SEK 600M with a SEK 7.7M deficit (municipal annual report 2025).
Lunds Konsthall.note: Lunds Konsthall is a unit of Lund municipality under the Kultur- och fritidsnämnden and has no accounts of its own. Neither the municipal annual report 2025, the committee page nor lundskonsthall.se gives a budget or result for the hall. Parent totals as printed: the committee's operating cost base was 'drygt 600 miljoner kronor' (just over SEK 600M) in 2025, and it reported a deficit of SEK 7.7M, about 1 percent of its income; the committee also runs libraries, sports facilities, the culture school and Stadshallen. Investment outlay for the committee was SEK 59.6M against a frame of 62.3M (p. 102). A web search for a separate budget line found nothing. The Konsthall's rebuild (SEK 86M, approved August 2026) is a capital project, not an operating figure.

Malmö Konsthall.basis: Malmö stad årsredovisning 2025: driftredovisning table for Kulturnämnd (PDF p. 154) and text on Kulturnämnden (PDF p. 168); no line names Malmö Konsthall.
Malmö Konsthall.line: No separate accounts for Malmö Konsthall; the city's culture committee had 2025 income SEK 168M, costs SEK 791M and net cost SEK 623M (city annual report 2025).
Malmö Konsthall.note: Malmö Konsthall is a unit of the city's culture administration (Kulturnämnden) and has no accounts of its own; the city annual report 2025 does not mention it by name and malmokonsthall.se publishes no budget or annual report. Parent figures in millions as printed: income 168 (166 in 2024), costs 791 (766), net cost 623 (624), surplus against budget 0.4, equal to 0.1 percent of the committee's grant; the committee reported 4M of unbudgeted grants for art purchases. The Swedish Inheritance Fund grant of SEK 6M for Studio Syd (2025-27) is from the pin text and was not checked here. A web search for a separate Konsthall budget line found nothing.

Bonniers Konsthall.basis: Company page for Bonniers Konsthall Handelsbolag, org. no. 969715-1927; no annual report is listed.
Bonniers Konsthall.line: No accounts found: Bonniers Konsthall is a partnership (handelsbolag) with no annual report listed on allabolag.se, and the Bonnier group reports do not mention it.
Bonniers Konsthall.note: The legal entity is Bonniers Konsthall Handelsbolag (org. no. 969715-1927, registered 2005-12-01, 20-49 employees, auditor Per Oskar Thorslund), a partnership, which in Sweden need not publish annual accounts; allabolag.se lists no annual reports and shows only a turnover band of SEK 3,000-4,999 thousand for 2025 (an interval from SCB, not a figure from accounts, so not used). The Albert Bonnier group annual reports 2025 (Swedish and English) and bonnier.com/finansiellt contain no line for the Konsthall or the Jeanette Bonnier or Maria Bonnier Dahlin foundations. Funding by the Bonnier group and the Jeanette Bonnier Foundation is as stated on the pin and could not be quantified.

Moderna Museet.basis: Årsredovisning 2025: resultaträkning p. 40; notes 1, 2, 3 pp. 47-48 (intäkter av anslag, avgifter, bidrag); balansräkning p. 42 (myndighetskapital).
Moderna Museet.line: FY2025 income SEK 271.4M: about 75 percent public (state appropriation 70 percent), 3 percent private including sponsorship, 22 percent earned (annual report 2025, pp. 40, 47-48).
Moderna Museet.note: Figures in the report are in thousands (tkr), converted to full units. Public 203,237,000 is state appropriation 191,084 plus grants from state agencies 420, from other public sector 10,865 and from EU institutions 868. Private 7,340,000 is sponsor income 1,070 plus barter agreements 1,648 plus 'bidrag från övriga' (grants from others, non-state) 4,622; the text of the report gives sponsorship and barter together as 2,692, the note lines give 2,718. Musée de Tahiti et des Îles – Te Fare Ia.line: FY2024 operating receipts XPF 258M: the government of French Polynesia subsidy of XPF 158.8M is about 62 percent; capital-section receipts of XPF 163.7M are excluded (provisional account).
Musée de Tahiti et des Îles – Te Fare Ia.note: Provisional account. Income and expenditure are the operating section only (recettes 258,045,699; depenses 231,868,847; result 26,176,852). The capital section (receipts 163,681,515 including a 30,807,231 capital subsidy; spending 72,551,888; result 91,129,627) is left out as one-off renovation money under the Contrat de projets. The printed subsidy total reads 89,607,231, which is a misprint: its two parts, 158,800,000 and 30,807,231, add to 189,607,231. The other 99.2M of operating receipts is not itemised (it can include carried-over surplus), so private and earned are null. Working capital 189,237,321 XPF is not net assets.

Fiji Museum.basis: Fiji Parliament standing committee report on the Fiji Museum annual reports for 2016/17, January-July 2016 and 2015: section 2.1 Financial Performance (printed p. 8) and the grant history (printed p. 11).
Fiji Museum.line: FY2016-17 revenue FJD 1.45M, including a government operating grant of FJD 354k, about 24 percent; the capital grant of FJD 233k is not counted (committee report).
Fiji Museum.note: Latest year with a total in anything read: the committee summarises the audited 2016/17 report (qualified audit opinion); later museum annual reports were not found online. Public is the operational grant 354,404; the report does not say whether the capital grant 232,988 is inside the revenue total of 1,454,043, so it is excluded and flagged. The report also gives 2018/19 grants of 697,525 operating and 500,000 capital (the funding text figures) but no totals for that year. The rest of revenue is not split, so private and earned are null. 2015 revenue was 957,957 against expenditure of 961,070 under a disclaimer of audit opinion. The Fiji Museum Act and the US Ambassadors Fund in the funding text are not covered by the report.

IAIA Museum of Contemporary Native Arts.n: IAIA Museum of Contemporary Native Arts
IAIA Museum of Contemporary Native Arts.basis: Parent only: Institute of American Indian Arts and Alaska Native Culture and Arts Development (EIN 85-0365964), year to 30 September 2025, IRS e-file XML object ID 202631949349301198 (TEOS batch 2026_TEOS_XML_07A): Part I lines 12, 18, 22; Part VIII lines 1d, 1e, 1h, 2g.
IAIA Museum of Contemporary Native Arts.line: No separate accounts for the museum; the parent IAIA reported FY2025 income USD 34.2M, of which government grants USD 22.1M, about 65 percent (Form 990).
IAIA Museum of Contemporary Native Arts.note: Figures are null because the museum is a unit of IAIA and files no accounts of its own. Parent totals, not the museum: total revenue 34,206,656; expenses 30,234,958; government grants (line 1e) 22,081,056; contributions (line 1h) 27,182,876 including 740,356 from related organizations; programme service revenue (line 2g) 6,194,116, of which student tuition and fees 2,982,779, room and board 1,824,171 and the only museum line, museum admissions and special events, 132,360; net assets 90,198,334. The 75 percent federal share and the 13.48M appropriation in the funding text are not lines in the return. The Ford Foundation (2020) and Art Bridges (2025) grants to the museum are not itemised.

Urban Shaman Contemporary Aboriginal Art.basis: CRA T3010 open data, 2024 List of charities, Urban Shaman Inc. (BN 893731034RR0001), fiscal period ended 31 March 2024: Schedule 6 lines 4200, 4350, 4500, 4510, 4540, 4550, 4560, 4620, 4640, 4700, 4950.
Urban Shaman Contemporary Aboriginal Art.line: FY2023-24 income CAD 503k: 76 percent federal, provincial and municipal grants, 7 percent gifts and charity grants, under 1 percent earned sales (T3010, Schedule 6).
Urban Shaman Contemporary Aboriginal Art.note: Public is federal 243,002 (line 4540) plus provincial 95,000 (4550) plus municipal 44,500 (4560), so the Canada Council, Manitoba and Winnipeg arts funds are all in. Private is tax-receipted gifts 3,893 (4500) plus amounts from other charities 31,679 (4510, mostly foundations) plus memberships 590 (4620). Earned is sales of goods and services 2,321 (4640). In none of the three: other income 75,714 (insurance claims and minor items) and interest 6,155. Net assets are computed from total assets 597,128 less total liabilities 307,055 (deferred revenue 201,308); the return does not print net assets. Expenses 484,905. The register page for the later year was not read; the CRA open data lags the register.

Buku-Larrnggay Mulka Centre.basis: ACNC 2024 Annual Information Statement dataset (data.gov.au), Buku-Larrnggay Mulka Incorporated (ABN 66 988 958 476), report period 1 July 2023 to 30 June 2024: revenue from government, donations and bequests, revenue from goods and services, all other revenue, total revenue, total expenses, net assets.
Buku-Larrnggay Mulka Centre.line: FY2023-24 income AUD 10.2M: 10 percent government revenue, under 1 percent donations, 76 percent goods and services, 14 percent other revenue (ACNC annual information statement).
Buku-Larrnggay Mulka Centre.note: Large charity with general-purpose financial statements. Public is revenue from government 1,007,065 (the IVAIS and NT Government support in the funding text). Private is donations and bequests 22,053. Earned is revenue from goods and services 7,738,991; the return does not break it down, and the funding text calls the centre an art centre. All other revenue 1,385,872 is in none of the three, because it can hold non-government grants such as the Ian Potter and Cotton On foundations without naming them. Employee expenses 1,742,857; surplus 633,139. The ACNC register pages did not load from this machine, so the AIS dataset was used; the FY2025 return is not yet in a published dataset.

Blak Dot Gallery.basis: ACNC 2024 Annual Information Statement dataset (data.gov.au), Blak Dot Gallery Incorporated (ABN 20 913 962 977), report period 1 July 2023 to 30 June 2024: revenue from government, donations and bequests, goods and services, total revenue, total expenses.
Blak Dot Gallery.line: FY2023-24 income AUD 178k: 99.8 percent government revenue; expenses AUD 212k, of which AUD 183k is grants and donations paid out (ACNC annual information statement).
Blak Dot Gallery.note: Small charity on a cash basis; the return gives revenue and expenses only and no balance sheet, so net assets are null. Public is revenue from government 177,393 (the Australian Government, Creative Victoria and Merri-bek Council in the funding text are not itemised). Private is donations and bequests 360. Earned is the reported revenue from goods and services, 0. Expenses are employee costs 28,469 plus grants and donations made 183,291; the 34,007 deficit is not explained in the return.

Sámi Center for Contemporary Art (Sámi D.n: Sámi Center for Contemporary Art (Sámi Dáiddaguovddáš)
Sámi Center for Contemporary Art (Sámi D.basis: Brønnøysund Register Centre accounts register, Stiftelsen Sámi Dáiddaguovddáš (org. no. 912625281), year 1 January to 31 December 2025, journal no. 2026544627: driftsinntekter, driftskostnad, salgsinntekter, sumEgenkapital.
Sámi Center for Contemporary Art (Sámi D.line: FY2025 operating revenue NOK 7.92M against operating costs of NOK 8.15M; the register shows no grant breakdown, so the public share is not stated (Brønnøysund accounts register).
Sámi Center for Contemporary Art (Sámi D.note: The register gives totals only: operating revenue 7,920,945 (2024: 9,176,674; 2023: 7,728,972), of which sales revenue 149,408; operating costs 8,149,847 including payroll 3,291,000; financial income 132,396 and costs 8,364; result for the year -104,870; equity 1,611,273 (audited, small-enterprise rules). The Sámi Parliament grant of 6.09M in the funding text is not in anything opened: the register has no grant line and a search of Sametinget budget documents did not find it, so public is null. The accounts PDF is not published through the open API.

Toi Māori Aotearoa.basis: Toi Maori Aotearoa Annual Report 2025, Financial Highlights, Group statement of financial performance (printed p. 52) and statement of financial position (printed p. 53), year to 31 December 2025.
Toi Māori Aotearoa.line: FY2025 group income NZD 1.16M: 88 percent goods-and-services revenue including Creative New Zealand funding (not split out), 5 percent member fees and donations, 7 percent interest (annual report 2025).
Toi Māori Aotearoa.note: Group figures (the charitable trust plus Toi Maori Limited and Toi Maori Market Limited). Public is null because the report prints no Creative New Zealand amount: grants sit inside revenue from providing goods or services, 1,024,915, mixed with earned income, so earned is null too. Private is donations 457 plus fees and subscriptions from members 53,912. Interest 83,394. The printed 2025 group total expenses reads 1,286,127, which repeats the 2024 figure; the three group expense lines (595,564, 506,488, 5,166) add to 1,107,218, which matches the printed surplus of 55,460, so 1,107,218 is used. The trust alone had revenue 1,135,147 and expenses 1,097,812. Net assets are 1,813,996 in the table and 1,813,993 in the text.

Foam Fotografiemuseum Amsterdam.basis: Foam Jaarverslag 2025, chapter 11 De cijfers, Jaarrekening 2025, Staat van baten en lasten (printed pp. 41-42).
Foam Fotografiemuseum Amsterdam.line: FY2025 income EUR 5.15M: 24 percent public subsidy (AFK and City of Amsterdam), 24 percent private contributions and sponsorship, 52 percent earned (annual report 2025, pp. 41-42).
Foam Fotografiemuseum Amsterdam.note: Public is subsidies from the Amsterdam Fund for the Arts (AFK) 1,079,833 plus other City of Amsterdam subsidies 134,749. Private is contributions from private funds 1,014,909 plus sponsorship income 234,500, which is also shown separately as sponsorship. Earned is public income (tickets and sales) 1,706,027 plus other income 975,404. The three add to total income 5,145,422. Operating result 182,424 plus interest 9,160 gives 191,538 (the narrative prints 191,583). The statement of baten en lasten is the only financial table in the report; no balance sheet is printed, so net assets are null (the text puts the general reserve at about 1.2M and the maintenance fund at 600k). VriendenLoterij, VandenEnde and Garanti BBVA sit inside the private lines.

Fotomuseum Winterthur.basis: Fotomuseum Winterthur Jahresbericht 2024, Jahresrechnung (audited extract, Swiss GAAP FER 21, Deloitte): Erfolgsrechnung pp. 44-45 and Bilanz p. 46.
Fotomuseum Winterthur.line: FY2024 income CHF 2.17M: 57 percent City of Winterthur and Canton of Zurich, 14 percent the Verein, 2 percent earned; the rest names no funder (annual report 2024, p. 44).
Fotomuseum Winterthur.note: The extract prints no total income, so income is the sum of its printed lines: exhibition income 32,130, exhibition support 241,390, third-party exhibitions 17,205, shop 3,911, contributions received 1,583,000, interest 6,693, other 15,889 and restricted contributions 265,383, which gives 2,165,601. Expenditure 2,246,327 is exhibition costs 392,854, collection costs 20,666, Zentrum 5,000, operating costs 1,750,201, depreciation 69,369 and net property result 8,237; income less expenditure matches the printed result of -80,725 within rounding. Public is City of Winterthur 460,000 plus Canton of Zurich 770,000. Private is the Verein Fotomuseum 300,000. Not counted in either: other contributions 53,000, exhibition support 241,390 and restricted contributions 265,383, which name no funder. Earned is exhibition income, third-party exhibitions and shop sales. Net assets are Total Organisationskapital. The live fotomuseum.ch site sits behind a Cloudflare human-verification check and was left alone; this is the archived copy of the 2024 report, and a 2025 report was not found.

International Center of Photography.basis: International Center of Photography (EIN 23-7412428), year to 30 June 2025, IRS e-file XML object ID 202600509349300025 (TEOS batch 2026_TEOS_XML_02A): Part I lines 12, 18, 22; Part VIII lines 1e, 1h, 2g, 10c; Part X net assets. Private is line 1h minus 1e.
International Center of Photography.line: FY2025 income USD 7.53M against expenses of USD 15.18M: about 2 percent government grants, 49 percent other contributions, 53 percent earned, mostly tuition (Form 990, Part VIII).
International Center of Photography.note: The three shares add to more than 100 percent because net event losses of 383,113 and investment losses reduce total income below the sum of the lines. Public is line 1e, 179,321. Private is line 1h 3,840,902 less 1e; it includes membership dues 138,340, fundraising-event contributions 930,296 (gross) and 345,970 non-cash. Earned is line 2g 3,852,955 (tuition and educational fees 3,183,705, admissions 438,859, licensing 143,358, collections 72,697, royalties 14,028) plus line 10c 122,294. Expenses 15,178,559 exceed income by 7,644,843; net assets 44,714,612. The funding text gives FY2023 revenue of about 8M and expenses of 15M, so FY2025 is similar. Sponsorship is not split out.

Almaty Museum of Arts.source_kind: report on targeted use of funds
Almaty Museum of Arts.basis: Corporate Fund Almaty Museum of Arts (BIN 210640000778), Report on the targeted use of funds for 2024, one-page statement in thousand tenge as printed: founder contributions, other receipts, uses of funds.
Almaty Museum of Arts.line: FY2024 receipts KZT 14.1bn: 79 percent founder contributions, 21 percent unnamed other receipts, all spent on building the museum, which opened in September 2025 (report on targeted use of funds).
Almaty Museum of Arts.note: Construction year, not an operating budget, flagged because owner capital distorts it; the four published reports (2021 to 2024) all cover the building project and no operating-year accounts exist yet. Amounts are converted from the printed thousand tenge: founder contributions 11,212,603.22, other receipts 2,902,000.00 (source not named), so income is those two, 14,114,603.22 thousand; the printed total received of 14,860,257.22 also counts the opening balance of 745,654. Spending 12,339,238.94 thousand: project construction 9,032,444.04, administration 781,670.52, fixed assets 2,525,124.39. Closing balance 2,521,018.28 thousand, a cash balance and not net assets. The report does not name the founder, so the Astana Motors link in the funding text is not confirmed here. Earlier founder contributions: 367,235 (2021), 11,095,035 (2022), 12,372,770 (2023), all in thousand tenge.

Museo de Arte Moderno de Medellín (MAMM).n: Museo de Arte Moderno de Medellín (MAMM)
Museo de Arte Moderno de Medellín (MAMM).basis: Corporacion Museo de Arte Moderno de Medellin, Estados financieros 2024 (estado de resultados, estado de situacion financiera, notes 15 to 17; thousand pesos) and Memoria economica 2024 (section 5, income by source); Informe de Gestion 2025 p. 26 for the composition table.
Museo de Arte Moderno de Medellín (MAMM).line: FY2024 income COP 9.45bn; the museum's own table gives 42 percent own income, 27 percent sponsorship and donations, 23 percent public bodies (informe de gestion 2025, p. 26).
Museo de Arte Moderno de Medellín (MAMM).note: Income is ordinary income net of returns 9,081,151 plus other income 345,791 plus financial income 20,248 (thousand pesos), which equals the memoria total of 9,447,189,947. Expenditure is the sum of printed costs and expenses, 9,580,144 thousand, giving the reported loss of 132,954. Private is donations 1,126,095,431 listed donor by donor in the memoria (Fundacion Suramericana 250M, Mineros 240M, Fundacion Fraternidad 194.4M, Colombiana de Comercio 100M, Fundacion MUV 100M and many individuals). Public and earned are null in the audited figures: the memoria says no grants were received in 2024 and books city, ministry and other public contracts, rentals, ticketing and sponsorship inside service income of 9,111,034 thousand, so they cannot be split. Store sales were 946,387 thousand. The composition table covers 2024 and 2025 shares of total income: 2024 own income 42, sponsorship and donations 27, Alcaldia de Medellin 15, Ministry of Culture 4, other public entities 4, international 2, other 4, Sura 2; 2025 own income 39, sponsorship and donations 22, Alcaldia 15, Promotora Cultural 9, Ministry 5, international 4, other public 4. Public 23 percent for 2024 is Alcaldia plus ministry plus other public entities. No FY2025 audited statements were published yet. Net assets are 26,572,502 thousand and include a 27.9bn property revaluation.

Museo Nacional de Etnografía y Folklore.n: Museo Nacional de Etnografía y Folklore (MUSEF)
Museo Nacional de Etnografía y Folklore.basis: Parent only: Fundacion Cultural del Banco Central de Bolivia, Estado de Recursos y Gastos Corriente Comparativo 2025 (printed p. 160) and Ejecucion Presupuestaria de Recursos 2025 (printed p. 155); scanned PDFs read as page images.
Museo Nacional de Etnografía y Folklore.line: No separate accounts for the museum; the parent foundation reported 2025 current resources of BOB 49.5M, of which BOB 44.8M, 91 percent, is transfers from the central bank (published statements).
Museo Nacional de Etnografía y Folklore.note: Figures are null because the Fundacion publishes consolidated statements for all its museums and centres, with no line for MUSEF. Parent totals, not the museum, in bolivianos: current resources 49,509,590.76 (sales of goods and services 4,468,995.77; other income 213,978.45; current transfers received from the public financial sector 44,826,616.54); current expenses 55,293,516.03; capital transfers received 17,361,757.11; budget execution total received 66,885,728.85. The transfers come from the Banco Central de Bolivia, a state-owned bank, and are neither counted as public nor as private here. The statements are scanned images, so the figures were read from page images.

Henry Art Gallery.basis: The Henry Gallery Association Inc (EIN 23-7052537), Form 990 for the year 1 July 2024 to 30 June 2025, IRS e-file XML 202611359349314906 (TEOS 2026_TEOS_XML_05A): Part I lines 12, 18, 22; Part VIII lines 1e, 1h, 2g, 10c, 12; Part IX line 25. Private is line 1h minus 1e.
Henry Art Gallery.line: FY2024-25 income USD 4.28M: about 61 percent government grants, 21 percent other gifts, under 1 percent earned; investment income adds 20 percent (Form 990, Part VIII).
Henry Art Gallery.note: The filer is the Henry Gallery Association, the support body of the Henry at the University of Washington. The return says the university pays some expenses and payroll costs (mostly managers' pay) directly, and those costs are not in these figures. Public is line 1e 2,607,486; the return does not name the grantors, so city, county, state and federal bodies are not split. Private is line 1h 3,508,645 less 1e; it includes federated campaigns 83,130, membership dues 9,482, fundraising-event contributions 445,397 and noncash gifts 13,177, and there is no separate sponsorship line. Earned is line 2g 18,434 (admissions 13,759, publication sales 4,675) plus line 10c 2,330. In none of the three: investment income 841,466, net fundraising events -145,177 and other revenue (insurance proceeds 50,250). Expenses exceeded revenue by 555,007. The pin's USD 4.8M matches expenses of 4,830,955.

Pulitzer Arts Foundation.basis: Pulitzer Arts Foundation (EIN 43-1752949), Form 990-PF for calendar 2024, IRS e-file XML 202523119349101977 (TEOS 2025_TEOS_XML_11C): Part I, column (a), lines 1, 3, 4, 6a, 11, 12, 26; Part II; Schedule B.
Pulitzer Arts Foundation.line: Calendar 2024 income USD 10.2M, about 90 percent contributions from Emily R. Pulitzer and 9 percent dividends; expenses USD 6.2M; no government grants stated (Form 990-PF).
Pulitzer Arts Foundation.note: A private operating foundation, so there is no Part VIII and no government-grant line; public is left null. Private is Part I line 1 contributions 9,182,217. Schedule B lists one contributor, Emily R Pulitzer, in four noncash entries described as adjustments of pledge discounts from 2011, 2014, 2015 and 2020, 6,182,000 in all (about 60 percent of income); the other 3,000,217 is not itemised. These are book entries on the founder's pledges, so the year's income is far above cash income; expenses are the cleaner measure. Dividends 882,361, interest 26 and net securities gain 158,629 are in none of the three. Earned is other program income 14,008 (Part I line 11); admission is free. Expenses are total operating expenses 6,184,760; no grants paid. Net assets are the Part II end-of-year figure 113,550,180 (total assets 113,990,307 less liabilities 440,127). The pin's USD 6.2M matches expenses.

Parrish Art Museum.basis: Parrish Art Museum Annual Report 2025, Financial Review, printed pp. 24-25: Revenue and Support, Operating Expenses, Non-operating Expenses, Net Assets.
Parrish Art Museum.line: FY2025 income USD 6.24M: about 10 percent government grants, 60 percent gifts, events and membership, 18 percent earned (tuition, admissions, shop, cafe); expenses USD 6.38M (annual report 2025, p. 25).
Parrish Art Museum.note: The financial review in the annual report is a summary of the statements; the audit report itself is not in the PDF, and the museum's financials page links earlier audited statements only up to 2021. Income is Total Revenue and Support 6,243,385. Public is government grants 653,091; the report credits the New York State Council on the Arts and school-district property taxes (Southampton and Tuckahoe) but does not split the amount. Private is contributions 2,309,834 plus benefit events net 881,911 plus membership 543,780; there is no separate sponsorship line. Earned is tuition and fees 639,617, admissions 171,146, museum shop net 75,984 and cafe net 269,799. In none of the four: investment income 172,485 and investment gains 525,738. Expenses are operating 5,471,125 plus non-operating (depreciation 848,210, loss on disposal 60,175, interest 1,166) 909,551. Net assets fell by 137,291. The Form 990 for 2024 (IRS XML 202533149349303893) shows a one-off noncash gift of 9,245,000 that inflates that year, so 2025 is the cleaner year; its 2023 return shows income 4,715,317 and expenses 6,149,125.

SECCA.basis: SECCA Foundation (EIN 56-0656890), Form 990 for the year 1 July 2022 to 29 June 2023, IRS e-file XML 202343189349317769 (TEOS 2023_TEOS_XML_11A): Part I, Part VIII, Part VI Schedule O. This is only the support foundation, not the museum.
SECCA.line: SECCA is a state museum division with no accounts of its own; its support foundation's last return (to June 2023) shows USD 1.11M of income and USD 1.26M of expenses.
SECCA.note: Figures left null because the museum is a division of the North Carolina Department of Natural and Cultural Resources and has no separate accounts, and no state budget line naming it was found; a search turned up only a whole-museum 'Museum of Art' line in the 2026-27 state budget form, whose classification is unconfirmed, and a 15M capital appropriation for the Winston-Salem campus in 2024. The SECCA Foundation, whose Schedule O says its sole purpose is to support the State entity that is SECCA, filed a return for the year to June 2023 that ends with net assets of 0 and reports a transfer from another organisation: revenue 1,111,449 (contributions 1,023,867 including federated campaigns 48,750 and noncash 650, programme revenue 39,380 for entry and exhibition fees, investment income 17,641, other 30,561), expenses 1,261,889 (programmes 591,498, management 100,437, fundraising 569,954). The return says the executive director is a state employee and the State, through the Department of Cultural Resources, has the final say on programme and operating policy. The state's own spending on the museum is not in these figures, so they would understate the museum's size and its public share. The Hanes family and Z. Smith Reynolds Foundation in the pin text give no amounts.

Francis Skaryna Belarusian Library and M.n: Francis Skaryna Belarusian Library and Museum
Francis Skaryna Belarusian Library and M.basis: Francis Skaryna Belarusian Library and Museum (charity 1161434), receipts and payments accounts for 1 January to 31 December 2025, approved 9 March 2026: Section A1 receipts, A3 payments, Section B assets, pp. 1-5 of the accounts.
Francis Skaryna Belarusian Library and M.line: Calendar 2025 receipts GBP 111k: about 88 percent donations and grants (not split by funder), 12 percent rent from a flat; payments GBP 106k (receipts and payments accounts, A1).
Francis Skaryna Belarusian Library and M.note: Small-charity receipts and payments accounts, cash basis, no statement of financial activities. Receipts are donations and grants 97,510.54 (monthly lists with no funders named, so it mixes public and private money and sits in neither field), rent and utilities contribution from the flat at 37 Holden Road 13,311 (counted as earned) and bank interest 233.98. The register's annual return field shows income from government grants of about 42.25k for 2025, but the accounts name no public body, so public is left null; the pin's 'no regular public or corporate funding' is not contradicted or confirmed by the accounts. Payments include 59,358.97 of building refurbishment and maintenance (a one-off project for the new museum room) and 39,555.41 for library acquisitions and projects. Net assets are not stated: the statement of assets lists cash 20,520.36, a Fidelity reserve fund 93,020.59 and the freehold at 37 Holden Road at a trustee estimate of 1,000,000 with no formal valuation, and no liabilities.

Musée d'Orsay.basis: Rapport d'activité 2025 de l'Etablissement public des musées d'Orsay et de l'Orangerie, Annexes 21 'Compte de résultat agrégé', printed pp. 134-135 (compte financier 2025: Charges, Produits); mécénat paragraph p. 79.
Musée d'Orsay.line: FY2025 income EUR 98.7M: about 32 percent state and other public subsidies, 68 percent own revenue, of which EUR 9.6M patronage collected (activity report 2025, pp. 79, 134).
Musée d'Orsay.note: The legal body is the public establishment of the Orsay and Orangerie museums (it also runs the Hébert museum), so the figures cover both museums. Income is total produits 98,682,695 and expenditure total charges 85,236,447, a surplus of 13,446,249. Public is subventions de l'Etat 31,143,257 plus autres subventions 359,992 (the report does not name the other grantors). 'Autres produits' 67,179,446 (ticketing, concessions, patronage, privatisations and the rest) are not itemised in the compte de résultat, so earned is null. Private is the patronage receipts the report gives as 9.6 million euros collected in 2025 (cash basis, rounded, over forty sponsors and partners; it includes corporate sponsorship, so no separate sponsorship figure). The report also gives partnership and brand revenue of 700,000, concessions 5 million and privatisations 700,000, not added. In cash terms (budget execution) total receipts were 104,199,245, of which public service subsidy 30,684,508, own receipts 61,602,681 and earmarked receipts 11,245,219; spending was 100.4M. The pin's 43M Caillebotte purchase by LVMH is not in the 2025 figures. Net assets are not given in the report.

Peggy Guggenheim Collection.basis: Solomon R. Guggenheim Foundation (EIN 13-5562233), Form 990 for calendar 2024, IRS e-file XML 202503179349302825 (TEOS 2025_TEOS_XML_11A): Schedule F Part I, Europe region, activity 'Peggy Guggenheim Collection' (1 office, 49 employees), total expenditures; Part I, VIII and X for the Foundation.
Peggy Guggenheim Collection.line: The Venice museum has no published accounts of its own; the Guggenheim Foundation's 2024 Form 990 shows USD 9.86M spent in Europe on the Peggy Guggenheim Collection (Schedule F).
Peggy Guggenheim Collection.note: Only expenditure is stated for the Venice museum: Schedule F gives 9,864,324 for programme services at the Peggy Guggenheim Collection, in US dollars for calendar 2024, with 49 employees; the Italian operations are taxed in Italy and the Foundation publishes no Venice income statement, and the museum's site has no financial page, so income, public, private, sponsorship, earned and net assets are null. Two other Europe lines on Schedule F, exhibitions 641,187 and Guggenheim Abu Dhabi 766,393, are not Venice. Parent totals for the Solomon R. Guggenheim Foundation, calendar 2024: revenue 88,200,362, expenses 84,882,538, contributions 40,080,599 (government grants 557,068, membership dues 3,493,742, noncash gifts 1,032,870), programme service revenue 34,459,412 (admissions 17,316,951, museum and programme collaborations 13,939,468, exhibitions 3,202,993), investment income and gains 10,969,130, net assets 122,805,503. The corporate sponsors in the pin text (Swatch, Mapei, Rubelli, Florim, Roberto Coin, Villa Sandi, EFG) give no amounts.

Beirut Art Center.basis: Beirut Art Center Annual Report 2025, Financial Statements 2025, printed pp. 36-37 (Expenses; Incomes; Balance).
Beirut Art Center.line: FY2025 income USD 385k: about 69 percent private (donors, sponsors, fundraising events), 19 percent institutions of mixed origin, 12 percent earned; expenses USD 312k (annual report 2025, p. 37).
Beirut Art Center.note: The statement is a cash-style list of outcomes and incomes in dollars, with no stated audit opinion in the report (audit and accounting cost 5,548). Net assets are total endowment funds 68,319,487, of which 22,351,847 is the founding fund. MAAT had 294,500 tickets issued in 2025.

National Art Museum of China.line: No separate figures for the National Art Museum of China; its parent ministry's 2024 final accounts show income CNY 8.44bn and spending CNY 8.29bn across 22 units (departmental accounts).
National Art Museum of China.note: The ministry's consolidated final accounts list the museum among its units and say central funds keep the National Library, the museum and the Arts and Crafts Museum running, with no amount for the museum. Parent totals as printed in 10,000 yuan: total income 844,188.08, total spending 828,605.63, opening carry-over 251,629.05, closing carry-over 229,918.96. The museum's own departmental accounts are published on namoc.org, which did not resolve from here, and a search for them found nothing, so no museum line was read. Donations of the Ludwig collection named in the pin are not income lines.

Mohatta Palace Museum.basis: Mohatta Palace Gallery Trust, financial statements for the year to 31 December 2016 (EY Ford Rhodes, signed 19 January 2018; scanned): statement of income and expenditure (PDF p. 5), notes 9 to 11 (PDF p. 13), balance sheet (PDF p. 4).
Mohatta Palace Museum.line: FY2016 income PKR 51.6M: about 29 percent Sindh government donation, 37 percent private donations, 34 percent other income, mostly interest; the latest audited accounts readable (statements, 2016).
Mohatta Palace Museum.note: The trust's site lists audited accounts for 2013 to 2018, but the 2017 and 2018 files return 'not found', so 2016 is the latest read. Public is 'other donations' 15,000,000 from the Government of Sindh Culture Department (2015: 5,000,000 from the Attorney General Sindh). Private is donations from private sources 19,230,426: 20 named donors, mostly companies and banks (for example Unilever 1.5M, Habib Bank 1.8M, United Bank 2.0M, Telenor 1.5M, Shell 0.8M), given for specific events and functions, plus a forfeited deposit of 421,500. Other income 17,389,660 includes 14,887,110 of profit on government securities and savings; the other 2,502,550 is not itemised, so earned is null. Expenditure 22,640,825 includes staff 11,832,554 and depreciation 2,386,093. Surplus 28,979,261. Net assets 185,711,312. The 2016 notes show no ticket-sales line.

Arab Image Foundation.basis: IRS e-file XML 202601439349300105 (TEOS 2026_TEOS_XML_06A), read from the IRS bulk zip; Arab Image Foundation Inc (Brooklyn, EIN 93-3283398), year to 31 December 2025: Part VIII lines 1e, 1h, 2g, 12; Part IX line 25; Part I line 22.
Arab Image Foundation.line: No accounts for the Beirut foundation; its US entity, Arab Image Foundation Inc, filed a 2025 Form 990 with revenue USD 58,859 and grants paid USD 85,000 (Form 990).
Arab Image Foundation.note: The only filing is by the US non-profit of the same name, a separate small entity (preparer a bookkeeping firm), not the Beirut institution; the Beirut foundation's site lists funders with no amounts and no annual report, as the pin says. US filing for 2025: revenue 58,859 (contributions 58,502 including dues 1,000; programme revenue 250; other 107), no government grants on line 1e, expenses 105,359 of which grants paid 85,000, net assets reported as 58,859. A 2024 return also exists but ProPublica has no parsed data for it. Because these are not the Beirut foundation's budget, no field is filled.

Latvian National Museum of Art.basis: Publiskais pārskats 2025, section 2.1 table 'Finanšu resursi izdevumu segšanai' and 'Izdevumi' (PDF p. 17), with text 2.1.1 on the same page.
Latvian National Museum of Art.line: FY2025 funding EUR 9.27M: about 85 percent state budget grant, 14 percent own revenue, 3 percent donations; the parts sum slightly above the stated total (public report 2025, p. 17).
Latvian National Museum of Art.note: Table (actual 2025): total resources 9,267,888; state budget grants (dotācijas) 7,845,596, of which building rent 2,142,754 for the Riga Exchange art museum and 382,712 for the Pulka street stores; paid services and other own revenue 1,292,333; transfers 100,000; donations and gifts 236,112. The four parts add to 9,474,041, which is 206,153 above the printed total, and the text gives own revenue as 1.9M while the table gives 1.29M, so the table is used and the gap is unexplained. Transfers 100,000 name no payer and are left out of public and private. Total spending 9,256,092 (running costs 8,964,867, capital 291,225). The report says funds also came from the State Culture Capital Foundation, the Ministry of Culture museum programme, EU programmes and private foundations and companies, without amounts. The collection is carried at 324,353,912 EUR, which is not net assets. The Italian Embassy, Riga City Council and Rietumu Banka backing of the show named in the pin are not itemised.

Museo de la Memoria y los Derechos Human.n: Museo de la Memoria y los Derechos Humanos
Museo de la Memoria y los Derechos Human.source_kind: Balance tributario (signed trial balance, not audited)
Museo de la Memoria y los Derechos Human.basis: Fundación Museo de la Memoria y los Derechos Humanos, Balance Tributario 1 January to 31 December 2025 (scanned, PDF pp. 2-3): accounts 4-1-01-xxx for income, column Ganancia; Memoria 2025 p. 6 for the state transfer.
Museo de la Memoria y los Derechos Human.line: FY2025 income CLP 2.49bn: about 96 percent public (state heritage service, presidential grant, Recoleta municipality), 1 percent donations, 2 percent rentals and collections services (trial balance, 31 Dec 2025).
Museo de la Memoria y los Derechos Human.note: Scanned trial balance, signed by the executive director and the accountant; no auditor's report was found on the museum's audits page. Public is the heritage-service project 2,355,033,047 (credits 2,400,025,999 less 44,992,952 held as a liability; the Memoria 2025 states a state transfer of 2,400,026,000) plus the presidential grant project 29,074,080 and the Municipalidad de Recoleta project 10,000,000. Private is voluntary contributions 33,124,733. Earned is rentals 37,165,164 and collections-area income 445,650. Named projects whose funder is not stated as public or private sit in neither field: ECCOM 17,296,890, MCI Argentina 6,963,264, Inter-American Court of Human Rights 1,170,254. Income is the sum of income-account credit balances and spending the sum of expense-account debit balances, so a monetary-correction loss of 12,609,990 and a Turkey project loss of 14,365 are inside expenditure; the matching December 2025 'Estado Financiero' nets them and shows operating income 2,477,648,727 and total 2,575,802,571. Net result is a deficit of 98,153,844 either way. The pin's 2.15bn is 2024; the 2025 transfer is higher. The 2025 memoria itself carries no accounts.

Kingston Creative.basis: Annual Report 2023, 'Financial Statements 2023': Profit and Loss (PDF p. 26) and the equity statement headed Statement of Financial Position (PDF p. 25), both scanned images in Jamaican dollars.
Kingston Creative.line: FY2023 income JMD 80.7M: local grants 35.0M, overseas grants 27.8M, core funding 11.9M, retail 6.1M; no funders named, so no public share (annual report 2023, p. 26).
Kingston Creative.note: The latest statements published; the 2024 and 2025 annual reports (read) are narrative with no financial statements. Revenue lines are Grant Funding Local 35,009,225, Grant Funding Overseas 27,772,540, Retail Income 6,058,013 and Core Funding 11,887,952. None names a funder or says whether it is public or private, so public and private are null; the pin's IDB Lab, Tourism Enhancement Fund, Ministry of Culture and corporate names are shown only as logos. Expenses exceed income by 9,662,053 (net deficit after interest 9,575,382); project expenses 73,572,337 and salaries 12,481,826. Total equity fell from 41,162,964 at end 2021 to 32,193,324 at end 2022 and 22,617,942 at end 2023. No auditor's report or notes are reproduced.

Beta-Local.basis: IRS e-file XML 202611279349300506 (TEOS 2026_TEOS_XML_05A), read from the IRS bulk zip; Beta-local Inc, EIN 66-0736115, year 1 July 2024 to 30 June 2025: Part VIII lines 1e, 1h, 2g, 12; Part IX line 25; Part I line 22.
Beta-Local.line: FY2024-25 revenue USD 328,157, all of it contributions and grants; no government grants, no programme or earned income (Form 990, Part VIII).
Beta-Local.note: All revenue sits in line 1f, other contributions 328,157; line 1e government grants is 0 and line 2g is 0. Funders are not itemised in the e-file (Schedule B is restricted), so the Mellon, Warhol and other foundation names in the pin were not matched to amounts. Prior years: FY2023 revenue 369,234, FY2022 362,451.

Barbados Museum and Historical Society.basis: Annual Report 2014 (year ended 31 March 2014; scanned): Statement of Income and Expenditure (printed p. 63) and Balance Sheet (printed p. 61), audited by Brian F. Griffith & Co.
Barbados Museum and Historical Society.line: FY2013-14 income BBD 1.96M: about 80 percent government subvention, 10 percent donations and memberships, 10 percent earned; the latest annual report posted (annual report 2014, p. 63).
Barbados Museum and Historical Society.note: The museum's financials page lists nothing later than the 2014 report, so these figures are twelve years old. Income lines: government subvention 1,555,465; donations 160,800, covenants 8,000, membership 34,746 (private 203,546); earned is educational programmes 8,967, special events 10,811, gate receipts 71,014, library and photocopies 4,140, museum shop net -1,661, professional fees 47,475, publications 11,260, other rentals 35,503 and reproduction services 2,174; interest 4,032 and sundry 2,312 are in neither field. Special events income is not split between fundraising and ticketed events. Spending 2,330,114 exceeded income by 375,076. Net assets 1,714,267, including fixed assets that rose from 208,416 to 1,918,565 and specific funds 528,633. The 2013 subvention was 1,757,890. The statement has no ground-rent or consulting-fee line, which the pin lists. The government's 2024-25 and 2025-26 Estimates (Program 276 Culture) fund the museum through a pooled grants item shared with other bodies and give no museum amount.

Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Cont.n: Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea
Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Cont.basis: Bilancio consuntivo 2022, nota illustrativa (getFile.php?id=897): table 'Entrate correnti' (PDF p. 5) and result section (PDF p. 44); competence figures from the DL 66/2014 prospect (getFile.php?id=898), entrate and spese correnti.
Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Cont.line: FY2022 current income EUR 4.62M: about 40 percent Ministry of Culture transfer, 53 percent earned (tickets, concessions, loan fees), 1 percent private; EUR 2.77M capital grants excluded (consuntivo 2022).
Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Cont.note: The latest outturn on the Galleria's budget page is 2022 (the page stops at a 2023 forecast); the museum's own transparency portal needs JavaScript and was not readable. Income is current revenue accrued 4,616,626.63; it leaves out capital grants from public administrations 2,766,000 (one-off investment money) and pass-through items 999,466.52. Public is the Ministry of Culture transfer 1,852,156.59. Private is 'contributi da privati' 50,000. Earned is ticket proceeds 908,570.00 (stated gross of the ticketing concessionaire's commission), concessions on assets 463,535.46 and loan-of-works fees 1,077,000.00 (one contract alone is 500,000); the fees are 23 percent of income. Insurance payments 27,450, refunds 237,914.04 and interest 0.54 are in neither field. Expenditure is current spending 3,849,346.01 (services 3,501,020.84, goods 69,417.39, pay 81,108.99, transfers to public bodies 131,742.65); capital spending of 2,797,454.00 is left out. The administrative surplus carried at end 2022 is 18,582,461.68, 95.58 percent of it earmarked; that is not net assets. Sponsors named in the pin (Autostrade, Enel) fall outside this year.

CaixaForum Madrid.basis: Not read: the foundation's financial-statements page returns a Cloudflare human-verification check.
CaixaForum Madrid.line: No figures read: CaixaForum Madrid has no separate accounts and its parent foundation's financial-statements page sits behind a human-verification check, which was left alone.
CaixaForum Madrid.note: CaixaForum Madrid is a centre of Fundación Bancaria la Caixa and has no accounts of its own. The foundation's site answers with a Cloudflare check ('Just a moment'), so it was left alone and no parent total was read; a search for the foundation's 2025 accounts found only CaixaBank dividend news and the accounts of a sister research foundation, not the parent. The pin's 2025 budget of EUR 655M (about 130M for culture and science) and the 947,642 visitors in 2024 were not checked against a document. Register route not found: the foundation's accounts are filed with the Spanish foundations protectorate, which was not opened here.

G.A.S. Foundation (Guest Artists Space).basis: Accounts of The Yinka Shonibare Foundation (charity 1183321, the UK sister of G.A.S.) for the year to 31 March 2025: trustees' report section g, statement of financial activities (PDF p. 16) and note 3.
G.A.S. Foundation (Guest Artists Space).line: No accounts for G.A.S. Foundation itself; its UK sister charity, the Yinka Shonibare Foundation, reported income GBP 315,397 and spending GBP 409,248 for the year to March 2025 (unaudited).
G.A.S. Foundation (Guest Artists Space).note: The register link in the pin leads to The Yinka Shonibare Foundation, a UK charity, not to G.A.S. Foundation, which is a non-profit in Nigeria and publishes no accounts. The UK charity fundraises for G.A.S., runs its programme and says the two share a close relationship. Its figures: income 315,397 (donations 189,368, grants 40,661, residency fees 60,565, art tours 24,553, interest 250), expenditure 409,248, total funds 79,630 (173,481 a year earlier). The Charity Commission shows no government grant income for 2025 and 17,500 for 2024. The UK accounts are marked unaudited. A Terra Foundation grant of 174,532 for multi-year work is deferred and not yet income. These are not G.A.S. figures, so no field is filled.
